bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第190卷卷第一百九十

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 190, Volume One Hundred Ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 190.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六】 起玄黓敦牂，盡閼逢涒灘五月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 6] It begins in the year Xuanhei Dunzhang and runs through the fifth month of the year Yanfeng Youtan; altogether a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 6] This section runs from the year Xuanhei Dunzhang through the fifth month of Yanfeng Youtan—a span of a little more than two years.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，劉黑闥自稱漢東王，改元天造，定都洺州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Liu Heita styled himself King of Eastern Han, changed the era name to Tiancao, and fixed his capital at Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Liu Heita declared himself King of Eastern Han, adopted the era name Tiancao, and made Mozhou his capital.

sentences.zh: 以范願為左僕射，董康買為兵部尚書，高雅賢為右領軍；

translations.literal: He appointed Fan Yuan as Left Vice Director, Dong Kangmai as Minister of War, and Gao Yaxian as Right Army Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fan Yuan as Left Vice Director, Dong Kangmai as Minister of War, and Gao Yaxian as Right Army Inspector;

sentences.zh: 征王琮為中書令，劉斌為中書侍郎；

translations.literal: he summoned Wang Cong as Director of the Secretariat and Liu Bin as Vice Director of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: he recalled Wang Cong as Director of the Secretariat and Liu Bin as Vice Director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 竇建德時文武悉復本位。

translations.literal: all civil and military officials from Dou Jiande's time were restored to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: and restored all of Dou Jiande's former civil and military officials to their previous ranks.

sentences.zh: 其設法行政，悉師建德，而攻戰勇決過之。

translations.literal: In establishing laws and administering government he wholly followed Jiande, yet in battle he was braver and more resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled his laws and administration entirely on Dou Jiande's, but in combat he proved bolder and more decisive than his predecessor.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，同安賊帥殷恭邃以舒州來降。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the bandit chief Yin Gongsui of Tong'an submitted Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Yin Gongsui, the rebel leader of Tong'an, surrendered Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，濟州別駕劉伯通執刺史竇務本，以州附徐圓朗。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Liu Botong, Vice Prefect of Jizhou, seized Prefect Dou Wuben and submitted the prefecture to Xu Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Liu Botong, vice prefect of Jizhou, arrested Prefect Dou Wuben and handed the prefecture over to Xu Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，東鹽州治中王才藝殺刺史田華，以城應劉黑闥。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Wang Caiyi, Administrator of Eastern Yanzhou, killed Prefect Tian Hua and surrendered the city to Liu Heita.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Wang Caiyi, chief administrator of Eastern Yanzhou, killed Prefect Tian Hua and opened the city to Liu Heita.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民軍至獲嘉，劉黑闥棄相州，退保洺州。

translations.literal: Prince Qin's army reached Huojia; Liu Heita abandoned Xiangzhou and withdrew to hold Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qin Li Shimin's army reached Huojia, Liu Heita abandoned Xiangzhou and fell back to defend Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 丙申，世民復取相州，進軍肥鄉，列營洺水之上以逼之。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Shimin recovered Xiangzhou, advanced to Feixiang, and pitched camp above the Mozhui River to press him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Li Shimin retook Xiangzhou, marched on to Feixiang, and encamped along the Mozhui River to hem Liu Heita in.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑既敗，散兵多歸林士弘，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: After Xiao Xian's defeat, scattered troops largely joined Lin Shihong, and his military strength revived.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Xian's defeat, many of his scattered troops rallied to Lin Shihong, and his forces grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 己酉，嶺南俚帥楊世略以循、潮二州來降。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Yang Shilue, a Li chieftain of Lingnan, submitted the two prefectures of Xun and Chao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Yang Shilue, a Li chieftain in Lingnan, surrendered the prefectures of Xun and Chao.

sentences.zh: 唐使者王義童下泉、睦、建三州。

translations.literal: The Tang envoy Wang Yitong subdued the three prefectures of Quan, Mu, and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang envoy Wang Yitong brought the three prefectures of Quan, Mu, and Jian under control.

sentences.zh: 幽州總管李藝將所部兵數萬會秦王世民討劉黑闥，黑闥聞之，留兵萬人，使范願守洺州，自將兵拒藝。

translations.literal: Li Yi, Regional Commander of Youzhou, led several tens of thousands of his troops to join Prince Qin Shimin in attacking Liu Heita. Heita heard of this, left ten thousand men with Fan Yuan to hold Mozhou, and personally led troops to oppose Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, regional commander of Youzhou, marched tens of thousands of his men to join Prince Qin in the campaign against Liu Heita. Hearing this, Heita left ten thousand troops under Fan Yuan to hold Mozhou and led his main force out to block Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 夜，宿沙河，程名振載鼓六十具，於城西二里堤上急擊之，城中地皆震動。

translations.literal: At night he encamped at Shahe. Cheng Mingzhen loaded sixty drums, rushed to a dike two li west of the city, and beat them furiously; the ground throughout the city shook.
translations.idiomatic: That night he camped at Shahe. Cheng Mingzhen hauled sixty drums to a levee two li west of the city and struck them in a furious roll; the ground inside the walls trembled.

sentences.zh: 范願驚懼，馳告黑闥；

translations.literal: Fan Yuan was alarmed and afraid, and galloped to inform Heita;
translations.idiomatic: Panicked, Fan Yuan sent a rider to warn Heita;

sentences.zh: 黑闥遽還，遣其弟十善與行台張君立將兵一萬擊藝於鼓城。

translations.literal: Heita hurried back and sent his younger brother Shishan and Regional Commissioner Zhang Junli with ten thousand troops to strike Yi at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Heita turned back at once and dispatched his brother Shishan and regional commissioner Zhang Junli with ten thousand men to attack Li Yi at Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 壬子，戰於徐河，十善、君立大敗，所失亡八千人。

translations.literal: On renzi they fought on the Xu River; Shishan and Junli were utterly defeated, losing eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi they fought along the Xu River. Shishan and Junli suffered a crushing defeat and lost eight thousand men.

sentences.zh: 洺水人李去惑據城來降，秦王世民遣彭公王君廓將千五百騎赴之，入城共守。

translations.literal: Li Quhuo of Mozhui seized the city and came to surrender. Prince Qin sent Duke of Peng Wang Junguo with fifteen hundred cavalry to go to him; they entered the city and defended it together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quhuo of Mozhui took the city and defected. Prince Qin sent Duke of Peng Wang Junguo with fifteen hundred horsemen to reinforce him, and they entered the city to hold it together.

sentences.zh: 二月，劉黑闥引兵還攻洺水，癸亥，行至列人，秦王世民使秦叔寶邀擊破之。

translations.literal: In the second month Liu Heita led troops back to attack Mozhui. On guihai, as he reached Lieren, Prince Qin had Qin Shubao intercept and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Liu Heita marched back to besiege Mozhui. On guihai, as he reached Lieren, Prince Qin sent Qin Shubao to ambush and rout him.

sentences.zh: 豫章賊帥張善安以虔、吉等五州來降，拜洪州總管。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Zhang Shan'an of Yuzhang submitted the five prefectures of Qian, Ji, and others, and was appointed Regional Commander of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shan'an, rebel leader of Yuzhang, surrendered five prefectures including Qian and Ji and was appointed regional commander of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，金鄉人陽孝誠叛徐圓朗，以城來降。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Yang Xiaocheng of Jinxiang rebelled against Xu Yuanlang and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Yang Xiaocheng of Jinxiang turned against Xu Yuanlang and surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 己巳，秦王世民復取邢州。

translations.literal: On jisi, Prince Qin Shimin recovered Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Prince Qin retook Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛未，并州人馮伯讓以城來降。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Feng Borang of Bingzhou surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Feng Borang of Bingzhou surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 丙子，李藝取劉黑闥定、欒、廉、趙四州，獲黑闥尚書劉希道，引兵與秦王世民會洺州。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Li Yi took the four prefectures of Ding, Luan, Lian, and Zhao from Liu Heita, captured Heita's Minister Liu Xidao, and led his troops to join Prince Qin Shimin at Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Li Yi seized the four prefectures of Ding, Luan, Lian, and Zhao from Liu Heita, captured Heita's minister Liu Xidao, and marched to join Prince Qin at Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥攻洺水甚急。

translations.literal: Liu Heita pressed the attack on Mozhui with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita pressed the siege of Mozhui with ferocious intensity.

sentences.zh: 城四旁皆有水，廣五十餘步，黑闥於城東北築二甬道以攻之；

translations.literal: Water surrounded the city on all four sides, more than fifty paces wide; Heita built two covered approaches northeast of the city to attack it;
translations.idiomatic: Water ringed the city on every side, fifty paces wide or more; Heita built two covered approaches from the northeast to assault the walls;

sentences.zh: 世民三引兵救之，黑闥拒之，不得進。

translations.literal: Shimin three times led troops to relieve it, but Heita blocked him and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: three times Li Shimin led relief columns, but Heita held him off and none could get through.

sentences.zh: 世民恐王君廓不能守，召諸將謀之，李世勣曰：「若甬道達城下，城必不守。」

translations.literal: Shimin feared Wang Junguo could not hold out, summoned the generals to deliberate, and Li Shiji said, "If the covered approaches reach the foot of the wall, the city surely cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wang Junguo could not hold the city, Li Shimin called his generals into council. Li Shiji said, "If those approaches reach the wall, the city is lost."

sentences.zh: 行軍總管郯勇公羅士信請代君廓守之。

translations.literal: Campaign General Duke of Yongluo Luo Shixin asked to replace Junguo in defending it.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign general Duke of Yongluo Luo Shixin volunteered to take Junguo's place in the defense.

sentences.zh: 世民乃登城西南高塚，以旗招君廓，君廓帥其徒力戰，潰圍而出。

translations.literal: Shimin then climbed a high mound southwest of the city and signaled Junguo with a banner; Junguo led his men in fierce fighting and broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin climbed a mound southwest of the city and waved a banner to summon Junguo. Junguo fought his way out through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 士信帥左右二百人乘之入城，代君廓固守。

translations.literal: Shixin led two hundred men on his left and right, rode in on their momentum, entered the city, and replaced Junguo in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shixin charged in with two hundred men at his side, entered the city, and took over the defense from Junguo.

sentences.zh: 黑闥晝夜急攻，會大雪，救兵不得往，凡八日，丁丑，城陷。

translations.literal: Heita attacked day and night with urgency. Heavy snow fell, and relief troops could not go; after eight days, on dingchou, the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Heita assaulted the city day and night without pause. Heavy snow blocked the relief columns. On the eighth day, dingchou, the city fell.

sentences.zh: 黑闥素聞其勇，欲生之，士信詞色不屈，乃殺之，時年二十。

translations.literal: Heita had long heard of his bravery and wished to take him alive; Shixin's words and bearing did not yield, so he killed him. He was twenty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Heita had long admired his courage and wanted him alive, but Luo Shixin refused to submit in word or bearing, so Heita had him executed. He was twenty years old.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，汴州總管王要漢攻徐圓朗杞州，拔之，獲其將周文舉。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Wang Yaohan, Regional Commander of Bianzhou, attacked Xu Yuanlang's Qizhou, took it, and captured his general Zhou Wenju.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Yaohan, regional commander of Bianzhou, attacked Xu Yuanlang's Qizhou, captured it, and took his general Zhou Wenju prisoner.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，延州道行軍總管段德操擊梁師都石堡城，師都自將救之；

translations.literal: On gengchen, Duan Decao, Campaign General of the Yanzhou Circuit, attacked Liang Shidu's Shibao Fortress; Shidu personally led troops to rescue it;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Duan Decao, campaign general on the Yanzhou circuit, attacked Liang Shidu's fortress at Shibao. Shidu marched out in person to relieve it;

sentences.zh: 德操與戰，大破之，師都以十六騎遁去。

translations.literal: Decao fought him and inflicted a great defeat; Shidu fled with sixteen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Decao routed him, and Shidu escaped with only sixteen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 上益其兵，使乘勝進攻夏州，克其東城，師都以數百人保西城。

translations.literal: The Emperor reinforced his troops and ordered him to press the victory and attack Xiazhou; he took its eastern city, and Shidu held the western city with several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reinforced his army and ordered him to press on to Xiazhou. He seized the eastern city while Shidu held the western quarter with a few hundred men.

sentences.zh: 會突厥救至，詔德操引還。

translations.literal: Just then Turkic relief arrived, and an edict ordered Decao to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Turkic reinforcements then arrived, and the emperor ordered Duan Decao to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，秦王世民拔洺水。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Prince Qin Shimin took Mozhui.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Prince Qin captured Mozhui.

sentences.zh: 三月，世民與李藝營於洺水之南，分兵屯水北。

translations.literal: In the third month Shimin and Li Yi encamped south of the Mozhui River and divided troops to hold the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Li Shimin and Li Yi encamped south of the Mozhui River and posted detachments along the north bank.

sentences.zh: 黑闥數挑戰，世民堅壁不應，別遣奇兵絕其糧道。

translations.literal: Heita repeatedly offered battle; Shimin held his walls and did not respond, and separately sent elite troops to cut his supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Heita repeatedly challenged him to battle, but Li Shimin kept his men behind the walls and sent raiding parties to sever the enemy's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，黑闥以高雅賢為左僕射，軍中高會。

translations.literal: On renchen, Heita appointed Gao Yaxian as Left Vice Director, and the army held a great feast.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Liu Heita named Gao Yaxian Left Vice Director, and the army held a grand banquet.

sentences.zh: 李世勣引兵逼其營，雅賢乘醉，單騎逐之，世勣部將潘毛刺之墜馬；

translations.literal: Li Shiji led troops to press their camp. Yaxian, riding drunk, pursued alone on horseback; Shiji's subordinate general Pan Mao speared him and he fell from his horse;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji advanced on the enemy camp. Gao Yaxian, drunk, galloped out alone in pursuit. Li Shiji's officer Pan Mao speared him and knocked him from his horse;

sentences.zh: 左右繼至，扶歸，未至營而卒。

translations.literal: his attendants came up in succession, helped him back, and before reaching camp he died.
translations.idiomatic: his escort caught up and helped him back, but he died before reaching camp.

sentences.zh: 甲午，諸將復往逼其營，潘毛為王小胡所擒。

translations.literal: On jiawu the generals again went to press the camp, and Pan Mao was captured by Wang Xiaohu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the generals pressed the camp again, and Wang Xiaohu captured Pan Mao.

sentences.zh: 黑闥運糧於冀、貝、滄、瀛諸州，水陸俱進，程名振以千餘人邀之，沉其舟，焚其車。

translations.literal: Heita transported grain from the prefectures of Ji, Bei, Cang, and Ying by land and water together; Cheng Mingzhen with more than a thousand men intercepted them, sank their boats, and burned their carts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita moved supplies from Ji, Bei, Cang, and Ying by land and water alike. Cheng Mingzhen ambushed the convoy with a thousand men, sank the boats, and burned the wagons.

sentences.zh: 宋州總管盛彥師帥齊州總管王薄攻須昌，征軍糧於潭州；

translations.literal: Sheng Yanshi, Regional Commander of Songzhou, led Qi Regional Commander Wang Bo to attack Xuchang and levied army grain at Tanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yanshi, regional commander of Songzhou, joined Qi regional commander Wang Bo in an attack on Xuchang and requisitioned army grain from Tanzhou;

sentences.zh: 刺史李義滿與薄有隙，閉倉不與。

translations.literal: Prefect Li Yiman had a grudge against Bo and closed the granaries and would not give any.
translations.idiomatic: but Prefect Li Yiman, who bore a grudge against Wang Bo, shut the granaries and refused.

sentences.zh: 及須昌降，彥師收義滿，系齊州獄，詔釋之。

translations.literal: When Xuchang surrendered, Yanshi seized Yiman and imprisoned him in the Qi prefecture jail; an edict ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuchang fell, Sheng Yanshi arrested Li Yiman and threw him into the jail at Qi prefecture. An edict then ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 使者未至，義滿憂憤，死獄中。

translations.literal: Before the envoy arrived, Yiman died in prison from grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger had not yet arrived when Li Yiman died in prison, consumed by grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 薄還，過潭州，戊戌夜，義滿兄子武意執薄，殺之；

translations.literal: Bo returned and passed through Tanzhou. On the night of wuxu, Yiman's elder brother's son Wuyi seized Bo and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: On his way back Wang Bo passed through Tanzhou. On the night of wuxu, Li Yiman's nephew Wuyi seized him and killed him;

sentences.zh: 彥師亦坐死。

translations.literal: Yanshi also was put to death on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: and Sheng Yanshi was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 上遣使賂突厥頡利可汗，且許結婚。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to bribe the Turkic Qaghan Jieli and also promised a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to bribe the Turkic qaghan Jieli and offered a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 頡利乃遣漢陽公瑰、鄭元□、長孫順德等還，庚子，復遣使來修好，上亦遣其使者特勒熱寒、阿史那德等還。

translations.literal: Jieli then sent back Duke of Hanyang Gui, Zheng Yuanshu, Zhangsun Shunde, and others. On gengzi he again sent envoys to renew friendly relations, and the Emperor also sent back his envoys Teli Rehan, Ashina De, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli then released Duke of Hanyang Gui, Zheng Yuanshu, Zhangsun Shunde, and the rest. On gengzi he sent envoys again to restore friendly relations, and the emperor in turn sent back the Turkic envoys Teli Rehan, Ashina De, and their party.

sentences.zh: 并州總管劉世讓屯雁門，頡利與高開道、苑君璋合眾攻之，月餘，乃退。

translations.literal: Liu Shirang, Regional Commander of Bingzhou, was stationed at Yanmen. Jieli joined Gao Kaidao and Yuan Junzhang in a combined attack on him; after more than a month they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shirang, regional commander of Bingzhou, held Yanmen. Jieli joined Gao Kaidao and Yuan Junzhang in a combined assault that lasted more than a month before they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以隋交趾太守丘和為交州總管。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Sui Administrator of Jiaozhi Qiu He was appointed Regional Commander of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Qiu He, the former Sui administrator of Jiaozhi, was appointed regional commander of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 和遣司馬高士廉奉表請入朝，詔許之，遣其子師利迎之。

translations.literal: He sent his Chief Clerk Gao Shilian to present a memorial requesting to come to court; an edict permitted it and sent his son Shili to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu He sent his chief clerk Gao Shilian with a memorial asking to come to court. The emperor assented and dispatched Qiu He's son Shili to escort him.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民與劉黑闥相持六十餘日。

translations.literal: Prince Qin Shimin and Liu Heita faced each other in stalemate for more than sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qin and Liu Heita faced each other in stalemate for more than sixty days.

sentences.zh: 黑闥潛師襲李世勣營，世民引兵掩其後以救之，為黑闥所圍。

translations.literal: Heita secretly sent troops to raid Li Shiji's camp. Shimin led troops to strike his rear to rescue him and was surrounded by Heita.
translations.idiomatic: Heita launched a night attack on Li Shiji's camp. Li Shimin marched to hit the enemy rear in relief and was himself surrounded.

sentences.zh: 尉遲敬德帥壯士犯圍而入，世民與略陽公道宗乘之得出。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde led stalwarts to break through the encirclement and enter; Shimin and Duke of Lueyang Daozong rode the momentum and got out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde led a band of warriors through the encirclement to reach them, and Li Shimin and Duke of Lueyang Li Daozong broke out on their heels.

sentences.zh: 道宗，帝之從子也。

translations.literal: Daozong was the Emperor's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong was the emperor's cousin.

sentences.zh: 世民度黑闥糧盡，必來決戰，乃使人堰洺水上流，謂守吏曰：「待我與賊戰，乃決之。」

translations.literal: Shimin judged that when Heita's grain was exhausted he would surely come to a decisive battle, so he had men dam the upper reaches of the Mozhui River and told the dam keepers, "Wait until I fight the bandits, then breach it."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin reckoned that once Heita's supplies ran out he would force a decisive battle, so he had the upper Mozhui River dammed and told the keepers, "Do not breach the dam until I am fighting the enemy."

sentences.zh: 丁未，黑闥帥步騎二萬南度洺水，壓唐營而陳。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Heita led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry south across the Mozhui River and drew up in battle array pressing on the Tang camp.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Liu Heita led twenty thousand foot and horse south across the Mozhui and drew up in battle order hard against the Tang camp.

sentences.zh: 世民自將精騎擊其騎兵，破之，乘勝蹂其步兵。

translations.literal: Shimin personally led elite cavalry to strike their horsemen, defeated them, and riding the victory trampled their infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin personally led his best cavalry against the enemy horse, broke them, and drove the rout straight through the infantry.

sentences.zh: 黑闥帥眾殊死戰，自午至昏，戰數合，黑闥勢不能支。

translations.literal: Heita led his troops in a desperate fight from noon until dusk; they clashed several times, and Heita's force could no longer hold.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita's men fought to the death from noon until dusk in several fierce clashes, but his line could no longer hold.

sentences.zh: 王小胡謂黑闥曰：「智力盡矣，宜早亡去。」

translations.literal: Wang Xiaohu said to Heita, "Wit and strength are exhausted; you should flee early."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaohu told Heita, "We have spent our last strength—you should flee while you can."

sentences.zh: 遂與黑闥先遁，餘眾不知，猶格戰。

translations.literal: He and Heita then fled first; the rest of the troops did not know and still fought hand to hand.
translations.idiomatic: He and Heita slipped away first. The rest of the army did not know and kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 守吏決堰，洺水大至，深丈餘，黑闥眾大潰，斬首萬餘級，溺死數千人，黑闥與范願等二百騎奔突厥，山東悉平。

translations.literal: The dam keepers breached the dike; the Mozhui River surged in more than a zhang deep. Heita's host collapsed in great disorder; more than ten thousand heads were taken and several thousand drowned. Heita with Fan Yuan and two hundred horsemen fled to the Turks, and all of Shandong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The keepers breached the dam, and the Mozhui rose more than ten feet deep. Liu Heita's army collapsed. More than ten thousand heads were taken and several thousand men drowned. Heita fled to the Turks with Fan Yuan and two hundred horsemen, and all of Shandong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 高開道寇易州，殺刺史慕容孝幹。

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao raided Yizhou and killed Prefect Murong Xiaogan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kaidao raided Yizhou and killed Prefect Murong Xiaogan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己未，隋鴻臚卿寧長真以寧越、鬱林之地請降於李靖，交、愛之道始通；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiwei, the Sui Director of Guests Ning Changzhen requested to surrender the lands of Ningyue and Yulin to Li Jing, and the routes of Jiao and Aizhou were first opened;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiwei, the former Sui director of guests Ning Changzhen offered to surrender the territories of Ningyue and Yulin to Li Jing, opening the routes to Jiao and Aizhou for the first time;

sentences.zh: 以長真為欽州總管。

translations.literal: Changzhen was appointed Regional Commander of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and Ning Changzhen was appointed regional commander of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 以夔州總管趙郡王孝恭為荊州總管。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong, Regional Commander of Kuizhou, was appointed Regional Commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong, regional commander of Kuizhou, was transferred to regional commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐圓朗聞劉黑闥敗，大懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanlang heard that Liu Heita had been defeated and was greatly afraid, not knowing what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Yuanlang heard of Liu Heita's defeat, he was terrified and could see no way forward.

sentences.zh: 河間人劉復禮說圓朗曰：「有劉世徹者，其人才略不世出，名高東夏，且有非常之相，真帝王之器。

translations.literal: Liu Fuli of Hejian said to Yuanlang, "There is one Liu Shiche whose talent and stratagem are unmatched in the age, whose fame towers in eastern Xia, and who moreover has an extraordinary countenance—truly the vessel of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fuli of Hejian urged Yuanlang, "There is a man named Liu Shiche whose talent is unmatched in this age, whose fame towers across the eastern lands, and who bears the look of something greater than an ordinary man—truly material for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 將軍若自立，恐終無成；

translations.literal: If the general sets himself up, I fear in the end there will be no success;
translations.idiomatic: If you proclaim yourself ruler, I fear you will never succeed;

sentences.zh: 若迎世徹而奉之，天下指揮可定。」

translations.literal: if you welcome Shiche and support him, the empire can be settled at a gesture."
translations.idiomatic: but if you welcome Liu Shiche and set him at the head, the realm could be won at a wave of the hand."

sentences.zh: 圓朗然之，使復禮迎世徹於浚儀。

translations.literal: Yuanlang agreed and sent Fuli to welcome Shiche at Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang agreed and sent Liu Fuli to bring Liu Shiche from Junyi.

sentences.zh: 或說圓朗曰：「將軍為人所惑，欲迎劉世徹而奉之，世徹若得志，將軍豈有全地乎！

translations.literal: Someone said to Yuanlang, "The general has been misled by others and wishes to welcome Liu Shiche and support him. If Shiche gets his way, will the general have any ground left intact!
translations.idiomatic: Someone else warned Yuanlang, "You have been led astray. If Liu Shiche rises to power, what place will be left for you?

sentences.zh: 僕不敢遠引前古，將軍獨不見翟讓之於李密乎？」

translations.literal: I dare not cite distant antiquity—has the general alone not seen Zhai Rang before Li Mi?"
translations.idiomatic: I need not reach back to distant antiquity—have you forgotten what became of Zhai Rang once Li Mi took charge?"

sentences.zh: 圓朗復以為然。

translations.literal: Yuanlang again thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang was persuaded once more.

sentences.zh: 世徹至，已有眾數千人，頓於城外，以待圓朗出迎；

translations.literal: When Shiche arrived he already had several thousand followers and halted outside the walls, waiting for Yuanlang to come out to welcome him;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shiche arrived he already had several thousand followers and camped outside the walls, waiting for Xu Yuanlang to come out and welcome him;

sentences.zh: 圓朗不出，使人召之。

translations.literal: Yuanlang did not go out but sent men to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang stayed inside and sent men to summon him in.

sentences.zh: 世徹知事變，欲亡走，恐不免，乃入謁；

translations.literal: Shiche knew affairs had changed and wished to flee, but fearing he could not escape, he entered to pay his respects;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiche sensed the trap and thought of fleeing, but fearing he could not escape, he went in to pay his respects;

sentences.zh: 圓朗悉奪其兵，以為司馬，使徇譙、杞二州。

translations.literal: Yuanlang stripped him of all his troops, made him Chief of Staff, and sent him to subdue the two prefectures of Qiao and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang stripped him of his troops, named him chief of staff, and sent him to subdue Qiao and Qi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 東人素聞其名，所向皆下，圓朗遂殺之。

translations.literal: Easterners had long heard his name; wherever he went all submitted, so Yuanlang then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His fame had long preceded him in the east, and every place he marched on submitted—so Xu Yuanlang had him killed.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民自河北引兵將擊圓朗，會上召之，使馳傳入朝，乃以兵屬齊王元吉。

translations.literal: Prince Qin Shimin was leading troops from Hebei to strike Yuanlang when the Emperor summoned him, had him enter court by urgent relay, and turned the army over to Prince of Qi Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qin was marching from Hebei to attack Xu Yuanlang when the emperor recalled him by urgent dispatch to court and handed the army over to Prince of Qi Li Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 庚申，世民至長安，上迎之於長樂。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Shimin reached Chang'an, and the Emperor welcomed him at Changle.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Li Shimin reached Chang'an, and the emperor received him at Changle.

sentences.zh: 世民具陳取圓朗形勢，上復遣之詣黎陽，會大軍趨濟陰。

translations.literal: Shimin fully set forth the situation for taking Yuanlang; the Emperor sent him again to Liyang to join the main army advancing on Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin laid out the plan for taking Xu Yuanlang in full, and the emperor sent him back to Liyang to join the main force advancing on Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，廢山東行台。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Eastern Shandong Regional Headquarters was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the Eastern Shandong regional headquarters was abolished.

sentences.zh: 壬申，代州總管定襄王李大恩為突厥所殺。

translations.literal: On renshen, Li Daen, Prince of Dingxiang and Regional Commander of Daizhou, was killed by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Li Daen, Prince of Dingxiang and regional commander of Daizhou, was killed by the Turks.

sentences.zh: 先是，大恩奏稱突厥饑饉，馬邑可取，詔殿內少監獨孤晟將兵與大恩共擊苑郡璋，期以二月會馬邑；

translations.literal: Earlier, Daen had memorialized that the Turks were suffering famine and Mayi could be taken. An edict ordered Palace Vice Director Dugu Sheng to lead troops to join Daen in attacking Yuan Junzhang, with a rendezvous at Mayi in the second month;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Daen had reported that famine had weakened the Turks and that Mayi could be taken. The emperor ordered palace vice director Dugu Sheng to join him in an attack on Yuan Junzhang, with a rendezvous at Mayi in the second month;

sentences.zh: 失期不至，大恩不能獨進，頓兵新城。

translations.literal: Sheng missed the deadline and did not arrive; Daen could not advance alone and halted his troops at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Sheng missed the rendezvous, and Li Daen, unable to advance alone, halted at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗遣數萬騎與劉黑闥共圍大恩，上遣右驍衛大將軍李高遷救之。

translations.literal: Qaghan Jieli sent tens of thousands of horsemen to join Liu Heita in besieging Daen. The Emperor sent Right Valiant Cavalry General Li Gaoqian to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Jieli sent tens of thousands of horsemen with Liu Heita to besiege Li Daen. The emperor dispatched Right Valiant Cavalry General Li Gaoqian to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 未至，大恩糧盡，夜遁，突厥邀之，眾潰而死，上惜之。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Daen's grain was exhausted; he fled by night, the Turks intercepted him, his host collapsed, and he died. The Emperor regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Relief had not arrived when Li Daen's supplies ran out. He broke out by night, was intercepted by the Turks, and perished when his force collapsed. The emperor mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 獨孤晟坐減死徙邊。

translations.literal: Dugu Sheng was punished by commuted death and exile to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Sheng's sentence was commuted from death to exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 丙子，行台民部尚書史萬寶攻徐圓朗陳州，拔之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Shi Wanbao, Minister of the Household of the Regional Headquarters, attacked Xu Yuanlang's Chenzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Shi Wanbao, minister of the household on the regional staff, attacked Xu Yuanlang's Chenzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，廣州賊帥鄧文進、隋合浦太守寧宣、日南太守李晙並來降。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the bandit chief Deng Wenjin of Guangzhou, the Sui Administrator of Hepu Ning Xuan, and the Administrator of Rinan Li Jun all came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Deng Wenjin, rebel leader of Guangzhou, together with the former Sui administrators of Hepu and Rinan, Ning Xuan and Li Jun, all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚寅，瓜州士豪王幹斬賀拔行威以降，瓜州平。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengyin, Wang Gan, a powerful local clansman of Guazhou, beheaded Heba Xingwei and surrendered; Guazhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengyin, Wang Gan, a local magnate of Guazhou, killed Heba Xingwei and submitted. Guazhou was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇忻州，李高遷擊破之。

translations.literal: The Turks raided Xinzhou; Li Gaoqian defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Turkic forces raided Xinzhou, and Li Gaoqian routed them.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛亥，劉黑闥引突厥寇山東，詔燕郡王李藝擊之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinhai, Liu Heita led the Turks to raid the east of the mountains; an edict ordered Prince of Yann Commandery Li Yi to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinhai, Liu Heita brought Turkic allies to raid Shandong. The emperor ordered Li Yi, Prince of Yann Commandery, to repel the invasion.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，吐谷渾寇洮、旭、疊三州，岷州總管李長卿擊破之。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Tuyuhun raided the three prefectures of Tao, Xu, and Die; Li Changqing, Regional Commander of Minzhou, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the Tuyuhun raided Tao, Xu, and Die prefectures. Li Changqing, regional commander of Minzhou, drove them back.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，遣淮安王神通擊徐圓朗。

translations.literal: On yimao, Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong was dispatched to attack Xu Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong was sent to attack Xu Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，劉黑闥引突厥寇定州。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Liu Heita led the Turks to raid Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Liu Heita again raided Dingzhou with Turkic support.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲申，為秦王世民營弘義宮，使居之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiashen, Hongyi Palace was built for Prince Qin Shimin and he was made to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiashen, Hongyi Palace was built for Prince Qin Li Shimin, and he took up residence there.

sentences.zh: 世民擊徐圓朗，下十餘城，聲震淮、泗，杜伏威懼，請入朝。

translations.literal: Shimin attacked Xu Yuanlang, took more than ten cities, and his fame shook the Huai and Si region; Du Fuwei was afraid and requested to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin attacked Xu Yuanlang, seized more than ten cities, and his renown shook the Huai and Si region. Du Fuwei, unnerved, petitioned to come to court.

sentences.zh: 世民以淮、濟之間略定，使淮安王神通、行軍總管任瑰、李世勣攻圓朗；

translations.literal: Shimin, seeing that the region between the Huai and Ji was largely pacified, had Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, Campaign General Ren Gui, and Li Shiji attack Yuanlang;
translations.idiomatic: With the Huai and Ji corridor largely secured, Li Shimin left Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, campaign general Ren Gui, and Li Shiji to continue the campaign against Yuanlang;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，班師。

translations.literal: On yiyou, he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, he marched the main army home.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，杜伏威入朝，延升御榻，拜太子太保，仍兼行台尚書令，留長安，位在齊王元吉上，以寵異之。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Du Fuwei came to court; he was invited up to the imperial couch, appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince, while still holding concurrently the post of Director of the Secretariat of the Mobile Commandery, kept at Chang'an, ranked above Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, to honor him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Du Fuwei arrived at court. The emperor seated him on the imperial couch, made him Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince while retaining his post as director of the secretariat on the mobile commandery staff, and kept him in Chang'an with precedence above Prince of Qi Li Yuanji—a mark of extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 以闞稜為左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Kan Ling was appointed General of the Left Elite Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ling was appointed general of the Left Elite Guard.

sentences.zh: 李子通謂樂伯通曰：「伏威既來，江東未定，我往收舊兵，可以立大功。」

translations.literal: Li Zitong said to Le Botong, "Now that Fuwei has come, the lands east of the Yangtze are not yet settled; if I go to gather our former troops, I can achieve great merit."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong said to Le Botong, "With Fuwei at court, the east of the Yangtze is still unsettled. If I go back and rally our old soldiers, we could win a great victory."

sentences.zh: 遂相與亡至藍田關，為吏所獲，俱伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they fled as far as Lantian Pass, were seized by officials, and both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: They fled together toward Lantian Pass, were captured by the authorities, and both were executed.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥至定州，其故將曹湛、董康買亡命在鮮虞，復聚兵應之。

translations.literal: When Liu Heita reached Dingzhou, his former generals Cao Zhan and Dong Kangmai, outlaws at Xianyu, again gathered troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita reached Dingzhou, his former generals Cao Zhan and Dong Kangmai, hiding out at Xianyu, rallied their forces to join him again.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以淮陽王道玄為河北道行軍總管以討之。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Prince of Huaiyang Li Daoxuan was made Campaign General of the Hebei Circuit to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Prince of Huaiyang Li Daoxuan was appointed campaign general on the Hebei circuit and sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 丙申，遷州人鄧士政執刺史李敬昂以反。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Deng Shizheng of Qianzhou seized Prefect Li Jing'ang and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Deng Shizheng of Qianzhou seized the prefect, Li Jing'ang, and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，隋漢陽太守馮盎承李靖檄，帥所部來降，以其地為高、羅、春、白、崖、儋、林、振八州，以盎為高州總管，封耿國公。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Feng Ang, Administrator of Hanyang under the Sui, responding to Li Jing's dispatch, led his command to surrender; his territory was made the eight prefectures of Gao, Luo, Chun, Bai, Ya, Dan, Lin, and Zhen; Ang was made Regional Commander of Gaozhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Geng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Feng Ang, Sui-era administrator of Hanyang, answered Li Jing's summons and submitted with his forces. His territories were organized into eight prefectures—Gao, Luo, Chun, Bai, Ya, Dan, Lin, and Zhen. He was appointed regional commander of Gaozhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Geng.

sentences.zh: 先是，或說盎曰：「唐始定中原，未能及遠，公所領二十餘州地，已廣於趙佗，宜自稱南越王。」

translations.literal: Earlier, someone had urged Ang, saying, "The Tang has only just settled the Central Plains and cannot yet reach far; the more than twenty prefectures you command are already more extensive than those of Zhao Tuo—you ought to style yourself King of Southern Yue."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier someone had urged Feng Ang: "The Tang has only just pacified the heartland and cannot yet reach this far. Your territory of more than twenty prefectures is already larger than Zhao Tuo's domain. You should proclaim yourself King of Southern Yue."

sentences.zh: 盎曰：「吾家居此五世矣，為牧伯者不出吾門，富貴極矣。

translations.literal: Ang said, "My family has dwelt here for five generations; those who served as regional lords have not gone outside my house—we have reached the height of wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang replied, "My family has lived here for five generations. Every regional lord has come from our house. We have already reached the summit of wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 常懼不克負荷，為先人羞，敢效趙佗自王一方乎！」

translations.literal: I always fear I cannot bear the burden and would bring shame on my ancestors—how would I dare imitate Zhao Tuo and make myself king over a region!"
translations.idiomatic: I have always feared I would fail to live up to that legacy and disgrace our ancestors. How could I imitate Zhao Tuo and set myself up as a regional king!"

sentences.zh: 遂來降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: So he submitted to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 於是嶺南悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon all of Lingnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With that, Lingnan was fully brought under control.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛亥，以洺、荊、交、并、幽五州為大總管府。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinhai, the five prefectures of Ming, Jing, Jiao, Bing, and You were made Grand Regional Commander headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai, Ming, Jing, Jiao, Bing, and You were made grand regional headquarters.

sentences.zh: 改葬隋煬帝於揚州雷塘。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui was reinterred at Leitang in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of the Sui was reburied at Leitang in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，吐谷渾寇岷州，敗總管李長卿。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Tuyuhun raided Minzhou and defeated Regional Commander Li Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the Tuyuhun raided Minzhou and defeated Li Changqing, regional commander of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 詔益州行台右僕射竇軌、渭州刺史且洛生救之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dou Gui, Right Vice Director of the Yizhou Mobile Commandery, and Qieluosheng, Prefect of Weizhou, to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Dou Gui, right vice director on the Yizhou mobile staff, and Qieluosheng, prefect of Weizhou, to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，突厥頡利可汗寇邊，遣左武衛將軍段德操、雲州總管李子和將兵拒之。

translations.literal: On yimao, Qaghan Jieli of the Turks raided the frontier; Left Martial Guard General Duan Decao and Regional Commander of Yunzhou Li Zihe were dispatched with troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Turkic qaghan Jieli raided the frontier. Duan Decao, general of the Left Martial Guard, and Li Zihe, regional commander of Yunzhou, were sent with troops to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 子和本姓郭，以討劉黑闥有功，賜姓。

translations.literal: Zihe's original surname was Guo; for merit in campaigning against Liu Heita he was granted the imperial surname.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zihe's original surname was Guo; he was granted the imperial surname Li for his service against Liu Heita.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，頡利十五萬騎入雁門，己未，寇并州，別遣兵寇原州；

translations.literal: On bingchen, Jieli entered Yanmen with a hundred fifty thousand horsemen; on jiwei he raided Bingzhou, and separately dispatched troops to raid Yuanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Jieli entered Yanmen with 150,000 horsemen. On jiwei he struck Bingzhou and sent a separate column against Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚申，命太子出幽州道，秦王世民出秦州道以御之。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Crown Prince was ordered out by the Youzhou route and Prince Qin Shimin out by the Qinzhou route to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the crown prince was ordered out along the Youzhou corridor and Prince Qin Li Shimin along the Qinzhou corridor to meet the invasion.

sentences.zh: 李子和趨雲中，掩擊可汗，段德操趨夏州，邀其歸路。

translations.literal: Li Zihe rushed to Yunzhong to make a surprise attack on the qaghan; Duan Decao rushed to Xiazhou to cut off their return route.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zihe rushed toward Yunzhong to strike the qaghan by surprise while Duan Decao drove toward Xiazhou to block the retreat.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上謂群臣曰：「突厥入寇而復求和，和與戰孰利？」

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Emperor said to the assembled ministers, "The Turks have invaded and yet again seek peace—which is more advantageous, peace or war?"
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the emperor asked his ministers, "The Turks have invaded and are now suing for peace. Which course serves us better—peace or war?"

sentences.zh: 太常卿鄭元璹曰：「戰則怨深，不如和利。」

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuansu said, "If we fight, resentment will deepen; peace is more profitable."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuansu, minister of ceremonies, said, "War will only deepen their resentment. Peace is the better course."

sentences.zh: 中書令封德彝曰：「突厥恃犬羊之眾，有輕中國之意，若不戰而和，示之以弱，明年將復來。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Feng Deyi said, "The Turks rely on a mob like dogs and sheep and look down on China; if we make peace without fighting and show weakness, they will come again next year.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilor Feng Deyi said, "The Turks rely on sheer numbers and hold China in contempt. If we make peace without fighting, we show weakness and they will be back next year.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為不如擊之，既勝而後與和，則恩威兼著矣。」

translations.literal: This subject humbly thinks it better to strike them; after victory, then make peace—thus both grace and authority will be displayed together."
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should fight. Once we have won, peace will display both magnanimity and power."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 己巳，并州大總管襄邑王神符破突厥於汾東；

translations.literal: On jisi, Xiangyi Prince Shen Fu, Grand Regional Commander of Bingzhou, defeated the Turks east of the Fen River;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Shen Fu, Prince of Xiangyi and grand regional commander of Bingzhou, defeated the Turks east of the Fen.

sentences.zh: 汾州刺史蕭顗破突厥，斬首五千餘級。

translations.literal: Xiao Yi, Prefect of Fenzhou, defeated the Turks and took more than five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi, prefect of Fenzhou, routed the Turks and took more than five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾陷洮州，遣武州刺史賀拔亮御之。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun captured Taozhou; Heluo Liang, Prefect of Wuzhou, was dispatched to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun took Taozhou. Heluo Liang, prefect of Wuzhou, was sent to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 丙子，突厥寇廉州；

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Turks raided Lianzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the Turks raided Lianzhou;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，陷大震關。

translations.literal: On wuyin, they captured Dazhen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, they seized Dazhen Pass.

sentences.zh: 上遣鄭元璹詣頡利。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Zheng Yuansu to go to Jieli.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zheng Yuansu to negotiate with Jieli.

sentences.zh: 是時，突厥精騎數十萬，自介休至晉州，數百里間，填溢山谷。

translations.literal: At this time several hundred thousand elite Turkic horsemen, from Jiexiu to Jinzhou, filled valleys for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, several hundred thousand Turkic cavalry stretched from Jiexiu to Jinzhou, filling the valleys for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 元璹見頡利，責以負約，與相辨詰，頡利頗慚。

translations.literal: Yuansu saw Jieli, rebuked him for breaking the treaty, and argued and questioned him in turn; Jieli was quite ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuansu confronted Jieli, accusing him of breaking their agreements. As they debated, Jieli was visibly abashed.

sentences.zh: 元璹因說頡利曰：「唐與突厥，風俗不同，突厥雖得唐地，不能居也。

translations.literal: Yuansu then persuaded Jieli, saying, "Tang and the Turks have different customs; even if the Turks gain Tang territory, they cannot dwell in it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuansu then pressed his case: "Tang and the Turks live by different customs. Even if you take Tang land, you cannot hold it.

sentences.zh: 今虜掠所得，皆入國人，於可汗何有？

translations.literal: What you plunder now all goes to your people—what does the qaghan get?
translations.idiomatic: Everything you loot goes to your followers. What does it profit you?

sentences.zh: 不如旋師，復修和親，可無跋涉之勞，坐受金幣，又皆入可汗府庫，孰與棄昆弟積年之歡，而結子孫無窮之怨乎！」

translations.literal: Better to turn the army back, restore friendly marriage ties—you can avoid the toil of long marches, sit and receive gold and silks, and all will enter the qaghan's treasury. How does that compare with casting aside the brotherly warmth accumulated over years and forging endless resentment for your descendants!"
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw now, renew the marriage alliance, and you can avoid this march, receive gold and silk while it all flows into your treasury. Is that not better than throwing away years of brotherly goodwill and bequeathing endless hatred to your descendants?"

sentences.zh: 頡利悅，引兵還。

translations.literal: Jieli was pleased and led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli was persuaded and marched his army home.

sentences.zh: 元璹自義寧以來，五使突厥，幾死者數焉。

translations.literal: Since Yining, Yuansu had been envoy to the Turks five times and several times nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yining era, Zheng Yuansu had been envoy to the Turks five times and had nearly lost his life on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳，交州刺史權士通、弘州總管宇文歆、靈州總管楊師道擊突厥於三觀山，破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guisi, Prefect of Jiaozhou Quan Shitong, Regional Commander of Hongzhou Yuwen Xin, and Regional Commander of Lingzhou Yang Shidao struck the Turks at Sanguan Mountain and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guisi, Quan Shitong of Jiaozhou, Yuwen Xin of Hong circuit, and Yang Shidao of Ling circuit defeated the Turks at Sanguan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 乙未，太子班師。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Crown Prince withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the crown prince withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 丙申，宇文歆邀突厥於崇崗鎮，大破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Yuwen Xin intercepted the Turks at Chonggang Town and inflicted a great defeat, taking more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Yuwen Xin intercepted the Turks at Chonggang and routed them, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，定州總管雙士洛等擊突厥於恆山之南，丙午，領軍將軍安興貴擊突厥於甘州，皆破之。

translations.literal: On renyin, Shuang Shiluo of Dingzhou and others struck the Turks south of Mount Heng; on bingwu, General-in-Chief An Xinggui struck the Turks at Ganzhou—both were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Shuang Shiluo and others defeated the Turks south of Mount Heng. On bingwu, General-in-Chief An Xinggui routed them at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥陷瀛州，殺刺史馬匡武。

translations.literal: Liu Heita captured Yingzhou and killed Prefect Ma Kuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita took Yingzhou and killed its prefect, Ma Kuangwu.

sentences.zh: 鹽州人馬君德以城叛附黑闥。

translations.literal: Ma Junde of Yanzhou rebelled with the city and joined Heita.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Junde of Yanzhou surrendered the city and defected to Heita.

sentences.zh: 高開道寇蠡州。

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao raided Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kaidao raided Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，詔齊王元吉討劉黑闥於山東。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, an edict ordered Prince of Qi Li Yuanji to campaign against Liu Heita in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiyou, Prince of Qi Li Yuanji was ordered to campaign against Liu Heita in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以元吉為領軍大將軍、并州大總管。

translations.literal: On renzi, Yuanji was made Grand General-in-Chief and Grand Regional Commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Li Yuanji was appointed grand general-in-chief and grand regional commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，貝州刺史許善護與黑闥弟十善戰於鄃縣，善護全軍皆沒。

translations.literal: On guichou, Prefect of Beizhou Xu Shanhu fought Liu Shishan, Heita's younger brother, at Shuxian; Shanhu's entire army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Xu Shanhu, prefect of Beizhou, fought Heita's brother Shishan at Shuxian. Xu Shanhu's entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，右武候將軍桑顯和擊黑闥於晏城，破之。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Right Martial Guard General Sang Xianhe struck Liu Heita at Yancheng and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Sang Xianhe, general of the Right Martial Guard, defeated Liu Heita at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 觀州刺史劉會以城叛附黑闥。

translations.literal: Prefect Liu Hui of Guanzhou rebelled with the city and joined Heita.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui, prefect of Guanzhou, surrendered his city to Heita.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇北平。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan raided Beiping.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以秦王世民領左、右十二衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Prince Qin Shimin was put in charge of the Left and Right Twelve Guards as Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Prince Qin Li Shimin was made grand general of the Left and Right Twelve Guards.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，行軍總管淮陽壯王道玄與劉黑闥戰於下博，軍敗，為黑闥所殺。

translations.literal: On yichou, Campaign General Prince of Huaiyang Li Daoxuan fought Liu Heita at Xiabo; the army was defeated, and Daoxuan was killed by Heita.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Prince of Huaiyang Li Daoxuan fought Liu Heita at Xiabo. His army was defeated and Heita killed him.

sentences.zh: 時道玄將兵三萬，與副將史萬寶不協；

translations.literal: At the time Daoxuan commanded thirty thousand troops and was at odds with his deputy Shi Wanbao;
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan commanded thirty thousand men but was at odds with his deputy, Shi Wanbao;

sentences.zh: 道玄帥輕騎先出犯陳，使萬寶將大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Daoxuan led light cavalry out first to strike the enemy line and ordered Wanbao to follow with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan led his light cavalry forward to engage the enemy and ordered Wanbao to follow with the main force.

sentences.zh: 萬寶擁兵不進，謂所親曰：「我奉手敕雲，淮陽小兒，軍事皆委老夫。

translations.literal: Wanbao held his troops and would not advance, saying to those close to him, "I received a personal edict saying, 'The boy of Huaiyang—the whole campaign is entrusted to me, the old man.
translations.idiomatic: Wanbao held his troops back and told his confidants, "I have a personal edict saying that this boy from Huaiyang is nominal commander only—the real authority is mine.

sentences.zh: 今王輕脫妄進，若與之俱，必同敗沒，不如以王餌賊，王敗，賊必爭進，我堅陳以待之，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Now the prince is rash and advances recklessly; if I go with him we will surely perish together. Better to use the prince as bait for the enemy—when the prince is defeated the enemy will surely rush forward in pursuit; I will hold a firm formation and wait, and crushing them is assured."
translations.idiomatic: The prince is reckless. If I go with him we will both be destroyed. Better to let him be bait. When he falls, the enemy will rush forward in pursuit. I will hold a solid line and crush them."

sentences.zh: 由是道玄獨進敗沒。

translations.literal: Because of this Daoxuan advanced alone and was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan advanced alone and was cut down.

sentences.zh: 萬寶勒兵將戰，士卒皆無鬥志，軍遂大潰，萬寶逃歸。

translations.literal: Wanbao drew up his troops to fight, but the soldiers had no fighting spirit; the army then collapsed in great rout, and Wanbao fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Wanbao tried to bring his men into battle, but they had lost all will to fight. The army broke and fled, and Wanbao escaped.

sentences.zh: 道玄數從秦王世民征伐，死時年十九，世民深惜之，謂人曰：「道玄常從吾征伐，見吾深入賊陳，心慕效之，以至於此。」

translations.literal: Daoxuan had repeatedly followed Prince Qin Shimin on campaigns; when he died he was nineteen years old. Shimin deeply mourned him and said to others, "Daoxuan often followed me on campaigns, saw me plunge deep into enemy lines, admired and imitated it, and came to this end."
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoxuan had fought beside Prince Qin on many campaigns. He was nineteen when he died. Li Shimin grieved deeply and said, "Daoxuan had seen me charge deep into enemy lines and wanted to do the same. That is how this happened."

sentences.zh: 為之流涕。

translations.literal: He wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: He wept openly for him.

sentences.zh: 世民自起兵以來，前後數十戰，常身先士卒，輕騎深入，雖屢危殆而未嘗為矢刃所傷。

translations.literal: From the time Shimin first raised troops, over dozens of battles before and after, he always led from the front, riding light cavalry deep in; though often in peril he had never been wounded by arrow or blade.
translations.idiomatic: Since raising his army, Li Shimin had fought dozens of battles, always leading from the front and riding deep into enemy lines. He had been in grave danger many times but had never been struck by arrow or blade.

sentences.zh: 林士弘遣其弟鄱陽王藥師攻循州，刺史楊略與戰，斬之，其將王戎以南昌州降。

translations.literal: Lin Shihong sent his younger brother, Prince of Poyang Yaoshi, to attack Xunzhou; Prefect Yang Lue fought him, beheaded him, and his general Wang Rong surrendered Nanchangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shihong sent his brother, Prince of Poyang Yaoshi, to attack Xunzhou. Prefect Yang Lue fought and killed him. His general Wang Rong then surrendered Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 士弘懼，己巳，請降。

translations.literal: Shihong was afraid; on jisi he requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shihong, unnerved, submitted on jisi.

sentences.zh: 尋復走保安成山洞，袁州人相聚應之；

translations.literal: Soon he fled again to hide in the Baocheng Mountain caves; the people of Yuanzhou gathered to join him;
translations.idiomatic: He soon fled again to the caves at Baocheng Mountain, where people of Yuanzhou rallied to him;

sentences.zh: 洪州總管若干則遣兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Moze Jiang, Regional Commander of Hongzhou, sent troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Moze Jiang, regional commander of Hongzhou, sent troops and crushed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 會士弘死，其眾遂散。

translations.literal: Just then Shihong died, and his followers dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shihong then died, and his followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王道玄之敗也，山東震駭，洺州總管廬江王瑗棄城西走，州縣皆叛附於劉黑闥，旬日間，黑闥盡復故地，乙亥，進據洺州。

translations.literal: When Prince of Huaiyang Li Daoxuan was defeated, Shandong was shaken in terror; Prince of Lujiang Wang Yuan, Regional Commander of Mingzhou, abandoned the city and fled west; prefectures and counties all rebelled and joined Liu Heita; within ten days Heita fully recovered his former territory; on yihai he advanced and occupied Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Daoxuan was defeated, Shandong was shaken. Prince of Lujiang Wang Yuan, regional commander of Mingzhou, abandoned the city and fled west. Prefectures and counties defected to Liu Heita. Within ten days Heita had recovered his old domain, and on yihai he took Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚辰，滄州刺史程大買為黑闥所迫，棄城走。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengchen, Cheng Daimai, Prefect of Cangzhou, pressed by Heita, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengchen, Cheng Daimai, prefect of Cangzhou, forced by Heita, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉畏黑闥兵強，不敢進。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Li Yuanji feared Heita's strong army and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, intimidated by Heita's strength, refused to advance.

sentences.zh: 上之起兵晉陽也，皆秦王世民之謀，上謂世民曰：「若事成，則天下皆汝所致，當以汝為太子。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor first raised troops at Jinyang, it was all Prince Qin Shimin's plan; the Emperor said to Shimin, "If the undertaking succeeds, the whole realm will be due to you—you shall be made Crown Prince."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor raised his banner at Jinyang, the plan had been Li Shimin's. The emperor told him, "If we succeed, the realm will be yours. You shall be crown prince."

sentences.zh: 世民拜且辭。

translations.literal: Shimin bowed and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin bowed and declined the offer.

sentences.zh: 及為唐王，將佐亦請以世民為世子，上將立之，世民固辭而止。

translations.literal: When he became King of Tang, the officers also asked that Shimin be made heir apparent; the Emperor was about to install him, but Shimin firmly declined and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan became King of Tang, his officers also pressed for Li Shimin as heir. The emperor was ready to name him, but Li Shimin refused again and the matter rested.

sentences.zh: 太子建成，性寬簡，喜酒色游畋；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jiancheng by nature was easygoing and plain, fond of wine, women, and hunting;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng was easygoing by nature, fond of wine, women, and the hunt;

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉，多過失；

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yuanji had many faults;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Li Yuanji was prone to misconduct;

sentences.zh: 皆無寵於上。

translations.literal: Neither enjoyed favor with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Neither enjoyed the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 世民功名日盛，上常有意以代建成，建成內不自安，乃與元吉協謀，共傾世民，各引樹黨友。

translations.literal: Shimin's achievements and fame grew daily; the Emperor often intended to replace Jiancheng with him; Jiancheng was inwardly ill at ease, and thereupon conspired with Yuanji to overthrow Shimin together, each recruiting and building factions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin's fame and achievements grew daily, and the emperor often thought of replacing Jiancheng with him. Jiancheng grew uneasy and conspired with Yuanji to bring Shimin down, each building a faction of allies.

sentences.zh: 上晚年多內寵，小王且二十人，其母競交結諸長子以自固。

translations.literal: In his later years the Emperor had many favored inner consorts; there were nearly twenty younger princes, and their mothers vied to cultivate ties with the elder sons to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor favored many consorts. He had nearly twenty younger sons, and their mothers competed to ally with the elder princes for protection.

sentences.zh: 建成與元吉曲意事諸妃嬪，諂諛賂遺，無所不至，以求媚於上。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji bent themselves to serve the various consorts, flattering, fawning, and bestowing gifts without limit, seeking to curry favor with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji courted the consorts with flattery and lavish gifts, doing whatever it took to win the emperor's affection.

sentences.zh: 或言蒸於張婕妤、尹德妃，宮禁深秘，莫能明也。

translations.literal: Some said they committed impropriety with Lady Zhang, Jieyu, and Lady Yin, Defei; the inner palace was deeply secret, and none could verify it.
translations.idiomatic: Some said they had illicit relations with Lady Zhang and Lady Yin. The inner palace was too closely guarded for anyone to confirm it.

sentences.zh: 是時，東宮、諸王公、妃主之家及後宮親戚橫長安中，恣為非法，有司不敢詰。

translations.literal: At this time the Eastern Palace, the various princes, the households of imperial princesses, and consorts' kinsmen rampaged through Chang'an, wilfully breaking the law; officials did not dare investigate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, the Eastern Palace, the princes, imperial princesses' households, and consorts' relatives ran roughshod over Chang'an, breaking the law at will while officials dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 世民居承乾殿，元吉居武德殿後院，與上台、東宮晝夜通行，無復禁限。

translations.literal: Shimin dwelt in Chengqian Hall, Yuanji dwelt in the rear court of Wude Hall; with the upper palace and Eastern Palace they passed back and forth day and night without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin lived in Chengqian Hall and Li Yuanji in the rear court of Wude Hall. They came and went to the main palace and Eastern Palace day and night without restriction.

sentences.zh: 太子、二王出入上台，皆乘馬、攜弓刀雜物，相遇如家人禮。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince and the two princes going in and out of the upper palace all rode horses and carried bows, blades, and miscellaneous items; when they met one another they used family courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the two princes entered the main palace on horseback, bearing bows, blades, and all manner of gear, and greeted one another with the ease of family.

sentences.zh: 太子令、秦、齊王教與詔敕並行，有司莫知所從，唯據得之先後為定。

translations.literal: Orders of the Crown Prince, instructions of the Princes of Qin and Qi, and imperial edicts all circulated together; officials did not know which to follow and could only decide by whichever arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Orders from the crown prince, directives from the Princes of Qin and Qi, and imperial edicts all circulated at once. Officials had no way to know which took precedence and could only obey whichever arrived first.

sentences.zh: 世民獨不奉事諸妃嬪，諸妃嬪爭譽建成、元吉而短世民。

translations.literal: Shimin alone did not attend upon the various consorts; the consorts all competed to praise Jiancheng and Yuanji and speak ill of Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin alone refused to court the consorts. They in turn praised Jiancheng and Yuanji at every turn and slandered Li Shimin.

sentences.zh: 世民平洛陽，上使貴妃等數人詣洛陽選閱隋宮人及收府庫珍物。

translations.literal: When Shimin pacified Luoyang, the Emperor sent several noble consorts to Luoyang to review Sui palace women and collect treasured goods from the storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shimin took Luoyang, the emperor sent several high-ranking consorts to select Sui palace women and claim treasures from the storehouses.

sentences.zh: 貴妃等私從世民求寶貨及為其親屬求官，世民曰：「寶貨皆已籍奏，官當授賢才有功者。」

translations.literal: The noble consorts privately asked Shimin for treasures and to seek offices for their kinsmen. Shimin said, "Treasures have all been registered and reported; offices ought to be given to the worthy and those with merit."
translations.idiomatic: The consorts privately asked Li Shimin for treasures and for appointments for their relatives. He replied, "The treasures have all been inventoried and reported to the throne. Offices belong to the worthy and the meritorious."

sentences.zh: 皆不許，由是益怨。

translations.literal: He refused all; because of this their resentment grew.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every request, and their resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 世民以淮安王神通有功，給田數十頃。

translations.literal: Shimin rewarded Prince of Huai'an Li Shengtong for his merit with several dozen qing of farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin rewarded Prince of Huai'an Li Shengtong for his service with several dozen qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 張婕妤之父因婕妤求之於上，上手敕賜之，神通以教給在先，不與。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang Jieyu's father, through the lady, requested it from the Emperor; the Emperor issued a hand-edict granting it; Shengtong, citing that his directive for the grant came first, would not yield it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang Jieyu's father asked the emperor through her for the land; the emperor issued a personal edict granting it. Shengtong refused, saying his own order to award the tract had come first.

sentences.zh: 婕妤訴於上曰：「敕賜妾父田，秦王奪之以與神通。」

translations.literal: Lady Jieyu complained to the Emperor: "An edict granted farmland to my father, but the Prince of Qin seized it and gave it to Shengtong."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jieyu complained to the emperor: "You granted my father that land by edict, but Prince Qin took it and gave it to Shengtong."

sentences.zh: 上遂發怒，責世民曰：「我手敕不如汝教邪！」

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon grew angry and rebuked Shimin, saying, "Is my personal edict not as good as your directive!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and scolded Li Shimin: "So my own hand-edict counts for less than one of your orders!"

sentences.zh: 他日，謂左僕射裴寂曰：「此兒久典兵在外，為書生所教，非復昔日子也。」

translations.literal: Another day he said to Left Vice Director Pei Ji: "This boy has long held command of troops abroad and is coached by bookish advisers—he is no longer the son he once was."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he told left vice director Pei Ji, "That boy has commanded armies in the field for years and now listens to every word his scholar-advisers whisper. He is not the son I once knew."

sentences.zh: 尹德妃父阿鼠驕橫，秦王府屬杜如晦過其門，阿鼠家童數人曳如晦墜馬，毆之，折一指，曰：「汝何人，敢過我門而不下馬！」

translations.literal: Yin Defei's father Ashu was arrogant and overbearing. Du Ruhui, an aide of the Prince of Qin's household, passed his gate; several of Ashu's household servants dragged Ruhui from his horse, beat him, and broke one finger, saying, "Who are you to dare pass my gate without dismounting!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin Defei's father Ashu was insufferably arrogant. When Du Ruhui, an officer of Prince Qin's household, rode past his gate, several of Ashu's servants yanked him from his saddle, beat him, and broke a finger. "Who do you think you are," they shouted, "riding past my gate without dismounting!"

sentences.zh: 阿鼠恐世民訴於上，先使德妃奏云：「秦王左右陵暴妾家。」

translations.literal: Ashu feared Shimin would complain to the Emperor and first had Consort Defei memorialize, saying, "The men about Prince Qin bully and insult my household."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Li Shimin would appeal to the emperor, Ashu had Consort Defei report first: "Prince Qin's attendants have been bullying my family."

sentences.zh: 上復怒責世民曰：「我妃嬪家猶為汝左右所陵，況小民乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor again angrily rebuked Shimin, saying, "Even my consorts' households are bullied by your attendants—how much more the common people!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned on Li Shimin in anger: "If even my consorts' families are bullied by your men, what hope is there for ordinary people!"

sentences.zh: 世民深自辯析，上終不信。

translations.literal: Shimin argued his case at length, but the Emperor ultimately did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin defended himself at length, but the emperor would not believe him.

sentences.zh: 世民每侍宴宮中，對諸妃嬪，思太穆皇后早終，不得見上有天下，或歔欷流涕，上顧之不樂。

translations.literal: Whenever Shimin attended banquets in the palace, facing the various consorts, he would think of how Empress Taimu had died early and never lived to see the Emperor gain the realm; sometimes he would sigh and shed tears, and the Emperor would look at him unhappily.
translations.idiomatic: At palace banquets, seated among the Emperor's consorts, Shimin would sometimes remember that Empress Taimu had died too soon to see her husband win the empire—and he would sigh and weep. The sight displeased the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 諸妃嬪因密共譖世民曰：「海內幸無事，陛下春秋高，唯宜相娛樂，而秦王每獨涕泣，正是憎疾妾等。

translations.literal: The consorts then secretly joined in slandering Shimin: "Good fortune that the realm is at peace; Your Majesty's years are advanced and you should enjoy yourself—but the Prince of Qin weeps alone at every gathering. He plainly loathes us.
translations.idiomatic: The consorts whispered together in secret to slander him: "The realm is at last at peace and Your Majesty's years are many—you ought to be enjoying yourself. Yet the Prince of Qin weeps by himself at every feast. He plainly despises us.

sentences.zh: 陛下萬歲後，妾母子必不為秦王所容，無孑遺矣！」

translations.literal: After Your Majesty's long life ends, we mothers and our sons will surely not be spared by the Prince of Qin—not one of us will remain!"
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty is gone, we and our sons will never survive under the Prince of Qin—not one of us will be left alive!"

sentences.zh: 因相與泣，且曰：「皇太子仁孝，陛下以妾母子屬之，必能保全。」

translations.literal: They wept together and added: "The Crown Prince is benevolent and filial; if Your Majesty entrusts us to him, he will surely preserve us."
translations.idiomatic: They wept together and went on: "The Crown Prince is kind and dutiful. Entrust us to him, and he will surely keep us safe."

sentences.zh: 上為之愴然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved to sorrow by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 由是無易太子意，待世民浸疏，而建成、元吉日親矣。

translations.literal: From this he put aside any thought of replacing the Crown Prince, grew gradually distant from Shimin, and saw Jiancheng and Yuanji more intimately with each passing day.
translations.idiomatic: From that point he abandoned any thought of changing the heir, grew steadily colder toward Shimin, and drew Jiancheng and Yuanji closer day by day.

sentences.zh: 太子中允王珪、洗馬魏徵說太子曰：「秦王功蓋天下，中外歸心；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Attendant Wang Gui and Palace Aide Wei Zheng urged the Crown Prince: "The Prince of Qin's achievements overshadow the realm; within and without, hearts turn to him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Attendant Wang Gui and Palace Aide Wei Zheng urged the Crown Prince: "The Prince of Qin's deeds outshine everyone under heaven, and the realm's loyalty runs to him.

sentences.zh: 殿下但以年長位居東宮，無大功以鎮服海內。

translations.literal: Your Highness relies solely on seniority to hold the Eastern Palace, without great merit to awe the realm into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness holds the Eastern Palace only because you are the elder son—you have no great victory to command the realm's respect.

sentences.zh: 今劉黑闥散亡之餘，眾不滿萬，資糧匱乏，以大軍臨之，勢如拉朽，殿下宜自擊之以取功名，因結納山東豪傑，庶可自安。」

translations.literal: Now Liu Heita's remnant forces number fewer than ten thousand, their supplies exhausted. A great army pressing upon them would collapse them like rotten wood. Your Highness should lead the strike yourself to win merit, and thereby forge ties with the great men of the east—thus you may secure your position."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita's broken army now numbers fewer than ten thousand men and his stores are empty. A major force sent against him would snap his resistance like rotten timber. Your Highness should take the field yourself, win glory in battle, and win over the great families of the east—that is how you may secure your own position."

sentences.zh: 太子乃請行於上，上許之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince then requested permission to take the field; the Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince asked the Emperor for leave to campaign, and the Emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 珪，頍之兄子也。

translations.literal: Gui was a nephew of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui was a nephew of Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔太子建成將兵討黑闥，其陝東道大行台及山東道行軍元帥、河南、河北諸州並受建成處分，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: On jiashen an edict ordered Crown Prince Jiancheng to lead troops against Heita; the Eastern Shaanxi Grand Secretariat, the Shandong campaign commander-in-chief, and all the prefectures of Henan and Hebei were placed under Jiancheng's disposal, empowered to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the Emperor ordered Crown Prince Jiancheng to take command against Liu Heita. The Eastern Shaanxi Grand Secretariat, the Shandong campaign headquarters, and every prefecture in Henan and Hebei were placed under his authority, with full power to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，封宗室略陽公道宗等十八人為郡王。

translations.literal: On yiyou eighteen members of the imperial clan including Prince of Lueyang Dao Zong were enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou eighteen members of the imperial clan, including Prince of Lueyang Li Dao Zong, were enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 道宗，道玄從父弟也，為靈州總管，梁師都遣弟洛兒引突厥數萬圍之，道宗乘間出擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Dao Zong was a younger cousin of Dao Xuan. As regional commander of Lingzhou, when Liang Shidu sent his brother Luo'er to lead tens of thousands of Turks in a siege, Dao Zong seized an opening to sally forth and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Zong was a younger cousin of Li Dao Xuan. While serving as regional commander of Lingzhou, he was besieged by tens of thousands of Turks led by Liang Shidu's brother Luo'er. Dao Zong found an opening, sallied out, and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 突厥與師都連結，遣其郁射設入居故五原，道宗逐出之，斥地千餘里。

translations.literal: The Turks allied with Shidu and sent their Yueshe she to occupy the old Wuyuan; Dao Zong drove them out and pushed the frontier back more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks joined forces with Shidu and sent their Yueshe she to occupy the old territory of Wuyuan. Dao Zong expelled them and extended Tang control more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 上以道宗武干如魏任城王彰，乃立為任城郡王。

translations.literal: The Emperor, finding Dao Zong's martial talent comparable to Cao Zhang, Prince of Rencheng of Wei, enfeoffed him as Prince of Rencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged Dao Zong's martial prowess equal to that of Cao Zhang, Prince of Rencheng of Wei, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Rencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 丙申，上幸宜州。

translations.literal: On bingshen the Emperor visited Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the Emperor traveled to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 己亥，齊王元吉遣兵擊劉十善於魏州，破之。

translations.literal: On jihai the Prince of Qi Yuanji dispatched troops to attack Liu Shishan at Weizhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Prince of Qi Li Yuanji sent troops against Liu Shishan at Weizhou and routed him.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，上校獵於富平。

translations.literal: On guimao the Emperor conducted a hunting review at Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Emperor held a hunting expedition at Fuping.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥擁兵而南，自相州以北州縣皆附之，唯魏州總管田留安勒兵拒守。

translations.literal: Liu Heita marched south with his army; from Xiangzhou northward every prefecture and county submitted to him—only Regional Commander Tian Liu'an of Weizhou mustered troops to resist and hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita marched south at the head of his army. From Xiangzhou northward, prefecture after prefecture and county after county went over to him—only Tian Liu'an, regional commander of Weizhou, gathered his forces and held firm.

sentences.zh: 黑闥攻之，不下，引兵南拔元城，復還攻之。

translations.literal: Heita assaulted it without success, led his men south to seize Yuancheng, then returned to attack Weizhou again.
translations.idiomatic: Heita attacked but could not take the city. He marched south, captured Yuancheng, then turned back to besiege Weizhou once more.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚戌，立宗室孝友等八人為郡王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengxu, eight members of the imperial clan including Xiaoyou were enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengxu, eight members of the imperial clan, including Li Xiaoyou, were enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 孝友，神通之子也。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou was Shengtong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou was the son of Li Shengtong.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，上校獵於華池。

translations.literal: On bingchen the Emperor conducted a hunting review at Huachi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the Emperor held a hunting expedition at Huachi.

sentences.zh: 戊午，劉黑闥陷恆州，殺刺史王公政。

translations.literal: On wuwu Liu Heita took Hengzhou and killed Prefect Wang Gongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Liu Heita captured Hengzhou and executed Prefect Wang Gongzheng.

sentences.zh: 庚申，車駕至長安。

translations.literal: On gengshen the imperial carriage arrived at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the Emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，幽州大總管李藝復廉、定二州。

translations.literal: On guihai Grand Regional Commander Li Yi of Youzhou recovered the two prefectures of Lian and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Li Yi, grand regional commander of Youzhou, recaptured the prefectures of Lian and Ding.

sentences.zh: 甲子，田留安擊劉黑闥，破之，獲其莘州刺史孟柱，降將卒六千人。

translations.literal: On jiazi Tian Liu'an attacked Liu Heita, defeated him, captured his Prefect of Shenzhou Meng Zhu, and received the surrender of six thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Tian Liu'an struck Liu Heita, routed his army, captured Heita's prefect of Shenzhou Meng Zhu, and accepted the surrender of six thousand officers and men.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東豪傑多殺長吏以應黑闥，上下相猜，人益離怨；

translations.literal: At this time many of the great men of the east killed their senior officials to join Heita; mutual suspicion ran between rulers and ruled, and popular alienation deepened.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many of the great families of the east were killing their magistrates to rally to Heita. Distrust ran between officials and people, and resentment only spread.

sentences.zh: 留安待吏民獨坦然無疑，白事者無問親疏，皆聽直入臥內，每謂吏民曰：「吾與爾曹俱為國御賊，固宜同心協力，必欲棄順從逆者，但自斬吾首去。」
