translations.literal: Liu'an alone treated officials and commoners with open trust. Petitioners, kin or stranger alike, were all admitted directly to his bedchamber. He often told officials and people: "We are all defending the realm against bandits and ought to stand together. If anyone wishes to abandon loyalty for rebellion, let him simply take my head first."
translations.idiomatic: Liu'an alone treated officials and commoners with unguarded trust. Petitioners, whether friend or stranger, were admitted straight into his bedchamber. He told them again and again: "We are all fighting for the realm against these bandits and ought to stand as one. If any of you mean to turn rebel, then take my head first."

sentences.zh: 吏民皆相戒曰：「田公推至誠以待人，當共竭死力報之，必不可負。」

translations.literal: Officials and commoners warned one another: "Lord Tian treats others with utmost sincerity; we must repay him with all our strength—not one of us may betray him."
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners warned one another: "Lord Tian meets us with perfect sincerity. We must repay him with our lives—not one of us may betray him."

sentences.zh: 有苑竹林者，本黑闥之黨，潛有異志。

translations.literal: There was one Yuan Zhulin, originally a partisan of Heita, who secretly harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: One Yuan Zhulin, formerly a follower of Heita, secretly nursed other ambitions.

sentences.zh: 留安知之，不發其事，引置左右，委以管鑰；

translations.literal: Liu'an knew of it but did not expose the matter; he brought Zhulin close and entrusted him with the keys.
translations.idiomatic: Liu'an knew of it but said nothing. He drew Zhulin close, kept him at his side, and entrusted him with the keys to the gates.

sentences.zh: 竹林感激，遂更歸心，卒收其用。

translations.literal: Moved with gratitude, Zhulin renewed his loyalty and in the end proved himself useful.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, Zhulin gave Liu'an his full loyalty and in the end proved invaluable.

sentences.zh: 以功進封道國公。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，并州刺史成仁重擊范願，破之。

translations.literal: On yichou Governor of Bingzhou Cheng Renzhong attacked Fan Yuan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Cheng Renzhong, governor of Bingzhou, attacked Fan Yuan and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥攻魏州未下，太子建成、齊王元吉大軍至昌樂，黑闥引兵拒之，再陳，皆不戰而罷。

translations.literal: Liu Heita's assault on Weizhou had not yet succeeded when Crown Prince Jiancheng and the Prince of Qi Yuanji arrived at Changle with a great army. Heita drew up his forces to meet them; they formed battle lines twice, each time dispersing without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita was still besieging Weizhou without success when Crown Prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji arrived at Changle with a great army. Heita drew up his troops to meet them. Twice the two sides formed for battle, and twice they withdrew without fighting.

sentences.zh: 魏徵言於太子曰：「前破黑闥，其將帥皆懸名處死，妻子系虜；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said to the Crown Prince: "When Heita was defeated before, his commanders were all condemned to death by published warrant, their wives and children held captive.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng told the Crown Prince: "When Heita was beaten before, his commanders were all sentenced to death by name, and their wives and children were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 故齊王之來，雖有詔書赦其黨與之罪，皆莫之信。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Prince of Qi came, though an imperial edict pardoned the crimes of his followers, none believed it.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, when the Prince of Qi arrived with an edict pardoning Heita's followers, none of them believed it.

sentences.zh: 今宜悉解其囚俘，慰諭遣之，則可坐視其離散矣！」

translations.literal: Now you should release all those prisoners, console them, and send them away—then you may simply watch them disperse!"
translations.idiomatic: Release every prisoner now, reassure them, and send them home—then you can simply watch Heita's forces melt away!"

sentences.zh: 太子從之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince took his advice.

sentences.zh: 黑闥食盡，眾多亡，或縛其渠帥以降。

translations.literal: Heita's grain ran out; many fled, and some bound their own commanders to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Heita's food ran out. Many of his men deserted, and some even bound their own commanders and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 黑闥恐城中兵出，與大軍表裡擊之，遂夜遁。

translations.literal: Fearing troops would sally from the city and strike him front and rear with the main army, Heita slipped away by night.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the garrison would sally out and crush him between city and field army, Heita fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 至館陶，永濟橋未成，不得度。

translations.literal: Reaching Guantao, he found the Yongji Bridge unfinished and could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: At Guantao he found the Yongji Bridge still unfinished and could not get across.

sentences.zh: 壬申，太子、齊王以大軍至，黑闥使王小胡背水而陳，自視作橋成，即過橋西，眾遂大潰，捨仗來降。

translations.literal: On renshen the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi arrived with the main army. Heita had Wang Xiaohu form a line with the river at his back, intending to cross west once the bridge was done—but his troops suddenly collapsed in rout, casting down weapons to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi arrived with the main army. Heita had Wang Xiaohu draw up his men with the river at their backs, planning to cross west as soon as the bridge was finished—but his army suddenly broke apart, casting down their weapons and surrendering.

sentences.zh: 大軍度橋追黑闥，度者才千餘騎，橋壞，由是黑闥得與數百騎亡去。

translations.literal: The main army crossed the bridge in pursuit of Heita, but only a little over a thousand horsemen had crossed when the bridge collapsed—thus Heita escaped with a few hundred riders.
translations.idiomatic: The main army crossed the bridge in pursuit, but only a little over a thousand horsemen had made it across when the bridge gave way—allowing Heita to escape with a few hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 上以隋末戰士多沒於高麗，是歲，賜高麗王建武書，使悉遣還；

translations.literal: Because many warriors of the late Sui had perished in Goguryeo, that year the Emperor sent a letter to King Gwangmu of Goguryeo ordering the return of all who remained;
translations.idiomatic: Because so many soldiers of the late Sui had died in Goguryeo, that year the Emperor wrote to King Gwangmu of Goguryeo demanding the return of all who remained there;

sentences.zh: 亦使州縣索高麗人在中土者，遣歸其國。

translations.literal: he also ordered prefectures and counties to search out Goguryeo people in the Central Plains and send them home.
translations.idiomatic: he also ordered prefectures and counties to find Goguryeo subjects living in the Central Plains and send them back to their country.

sentences.zh: 建武奉詔，遣還中國民前後以萬數。

translations.literal: Gwangmu obeyed the edict and repatriated Chinese subjects numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Gwangmu obeyed, and over time sent back Chinese subjects numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己卯，劉黑闥所署饒州刺史諸葛德威執黑闥，舉城降。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, on jimao Zhuge Dewei, Heita's appointed prefect of Raozhou, seized Heita and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on jimao Zhuge Dewei, the prefect of Raozhou appointed by Liu Heita, seized Heita and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 時太子遣騎將劉弘基追黑闥，黑闥為官軍所迫，奔走不得休息，至饒陽，從者才百餘人，餒甚。

translations.literal: At the time the Crown Prince had sent cavalry general Liu Hongji in pursuit. Hard pressed by government troops, Heita could not rest; reaching Raoyang he had only a little over a hundred followers and was famished.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince had sent cavalry general Liu Hongji in pursuit. Harried by government troops and unable to rest, Heita reached Raoyang with barely a hundred men left and was starving.

sentences.zh: 德威出迎，延黑闥入城，黑闥不可；

translations.literal: Dewei came out to welcome him and urged him to enter the city, but Heita refused.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei came out to meet him and urged him to enter the city, but Heita would not.

sentences.zh: 德威涕泣固請，黑闥乃從之。

translations.literal: Dewei wept and pleaded firmly; Heita at last agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei wept and pleaded until Heita at last consented.

sentences.zh: 至城旁市中憩止，德威饋之食；

translations.literal: They rested in the market beside the city walls, and Dewei brought them food.
translations.idiomatic: They halted in the market outside the walls, and Dewei brought them food.

sentences.zh: 食未畢，德威勒兵執之，送詣太子，並其弟十善斬於洺州。

translations.literal: Before the meal was finished, Dewei mustered troops and seized him, sent him to the Crown Prince, and together with his brother Shishan he was executed at Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before they had finished eating, Dewei called up his troops, seized Heita, and sent him to the Crown Prince. He and his brother Shishan were beheaded at Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 黑闥臨刑歎曰：「我幸在家鉏菜，為高雅賢罪所誤至此！」

translations.literal: At the execution Heita sighed: "I was fortunate enough to hoe vegetables at home, yet Gao Yaxian's crime misled me to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Heita sighed: "I was content hoeing vegetables at home—Gao Yaxian's folly is what brought me to this!"

sentences.zh: 壬午，巂州人王摩沙舉兵，自稱元帥，改元進通；

translations.literal: On renwu Wang Mosha of Qizhou raised troops, styled himself commander-in-chief, and declared the era name Jintong;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Wang Mosha of Qizhou raised an army, proclaimed himself commander-in-chief, and adopted the era name Jintong;

sentences.zh: 遣驃騎將軍衛彥討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched General of Agile Cavalry Wei Yan to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent General of Agile Cavalry Wei Yan to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以吳王杜伏威為太保。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Prince of Wu Du Fuwei was appointed Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Du Fuwei, Prince of Wu, was appointed Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚戌，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengxu, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengxu, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，還宮。

translations.literal: On jiayin he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 平陽昭公主薨。

translations.literal: Princess Zhao of Pingyang died.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Zhao of Pingyang died.

sentences.zh: 戊午，葬公主。

translations.literal: On wuwu the princess was buried.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the princess was buried.

sentences.zh: 詔加前後部鼓吹、班劍四十人，武賁甲卒。

translations.literal: An edict added front and rear military bands, forty ceremonial guards with drawn swords, and armored Tiger Guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted her funeral honors of front and rear military bands, forty ceremonial sword-bearers, and armored Tiger Guard soldiers.

sentences.zh: 太常奏：「禮，婦人無鼓吹。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies reported: "By ritual, women receive no military bands."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies objected: "By ritual, no woman is granted military bands."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「鼓吹，軍樂也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Military bands are martial music.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "Military bands are the music of war.

sentences.zh: 公主親執金鼓，興義兵以輔成大業，豈與常婦人比乎！」

translations.literal: The princess herself took up drum and gong and raised righteous troops to help complete the great enterprise—how can she be compared to ordinary women!"
translations.idiomatic: The princess herself took up drum and gong and raised righteous troops to help win the empire—how can she be compared to ordinary women!"

sentences.zh: 丙寅，徐圓朗窮蹙，與數騎棄城走，為野人所殺，其地悉平。

translations.literal: On bingyin Xu Yuanlang, brought to desperate straits, fled the city with a few horsemen and was killed by villagers; his territory was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Xu Yuanlang, driven to desperation, abandoned his city with a few horsemen and was killed by villagers. His territory was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 林邑王梵志遣使入貢。

translations.literal: King Fan Zhi of Linyi sent envoys to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Fan Zhi of Linyi sent envoys to pay tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 初，隋人破林邑，分其地為三郡。

translations.literal: Previously, when the Sui had smashed Linyi, they divided its land into three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Sui had conquered Linyi, they divided its territory into three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 及中原喪亂，林邑復國，至是始入貢。

translations.literal: When the Central Plain fell into chaos Linyi restored its kingdom; only now did it first send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Plains fell into chaos, Linyi restored its kingdom. Only now did it send tribute again.

sentences.zh: 幽州總管李藝請入朝；

translations.literal: Regional Commander Li Yi of Youzhou requested permission to attend court;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, regional commander of Youzhou, asked leave to come to court;

sentences.zh: 庚午，以藝為左翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On gengwu Yi was appointed Grand General of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he was appointed Grand General of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 廢參旗等十二軍。

translations.literal: The twelve armies including Canqi were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve armies, including Canqi, were abolished.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸未，高開道掠文安、魯城，驃騎將軍平善政邀擊，破之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guiwei, Gao Kaidao raided Wen'an and Lucheng; General of Agile Cavalry Ping Shanzheng intercepted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guiwei, Gao Kaidao raided Wen'an and Lucheng. General of Agile Cavalry Ping Shanzheng intercepted him and routed his force.

sentences.zh: 庚子，梁師都將賀遂、索同以所部十二州來降。

translations.literal: On gengzi Liang Shidu's generals He Sui and Suo Tong surrendered the twelve prefectures under their command.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Liang Shidu's generals He Sui and Suo Tong surrendered the twelve prefectures under their command.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，前洪州總管張善安反，遣舒州總管張鎮周等擊之。

translations.literal: On yisi former Regional Commander Zhang Shan'an rebelled; the Emperor dispatched Regional Commander Zhang Zhenzhou of Shuzhou and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi former regional commander Zhang Shan'an rebelled. The Emperor sent Zhang Zhenzhou, regional commander of Shuzhou, and others against him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，吐谷渾寇芳州，刺史房當樹奔松州。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, Tuyuhun raided Fangzhou; Prefect Fang Dangshu fled to Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Tuyuhun raided Fangzhou. Prefect Fang Dangshu fled to Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 張善安陷孫州，執總管王戎而去。

translations.literal: Zhang Shan'an took Sunzhou and seized Regional Commander Wang Rong away with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shan'an captured Sunzhou and took regional commander Wang Rong away as his prisoner.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，鄜州道行軍總管段德操擊梁師都，至夏州，俘其民畜而還。

translations.literal: On yichou Campaign Commander Duan Decao of the Fuzhou Circuit attacked Liang Shidu, reached Xizhou, captured its people and livestock, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Duan Decao, campaign commander of the Fuzhou circuit, attacked Liang Shidu, reached Xizhou, seized its people and livestock, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，吐谷渾寇洮、岷二州。

translations.literal: On bingyin Tuyuhun raided the two prefectures of Tao and Min.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Tuyuhun raided the prefectures of Tao and Min.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，南州刺史龐孝恭、南越州民寧道明、高州首領馮暄俱反，陷南越州，進攻姜州；

translations.literal: On dingmao Prefect Pang Xiaogong of Nanzhou, the commoner Ning Daoming of Nanyuezhou, and the chieftain Feng Xuan of Gaozhou all rebelled together, took Nanyuezhou, and pressed the attack on Jiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Prefect Pang Xiaogong of Nanzhou, the commoner Ning Daoming of Nanyuezhou, and the chieftain Feng Xuan of Gaozhou all rebelled together, captured Nanyuezhou, and advanced against Jiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 合州刺史寧純引兵救之。

translations.literal: Prefect Ning Chun of Hezhou led troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Chun, prefect of Hezhou, led troops to the relief.

sentences.zh: 壬申，立皇子元軌為蜀王、鳳為豳王、元慶為漢王。

translations.literal: On renshen the princes Yuan Gui was made Prince of Shu, Feng Prince of Bin, and Yuanqing Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the princes Yuan Gui, Feng, and Yuanqing were enfeoffed as Princes of Shu, Bin, and Han respectively.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以裴寂為左僕射，蕭瑀為右僕射，楊恭仁為吏部尚書兼中書令，封德彝為中書令。

translations.literal: On guiyou Pei Ji was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief, Xiao Yu Right Censor-in-Chief, Yang Gongren Minister of Personnel concurrently Director of the Secretariat, and Feng Deyi Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Pei Ji was made Left Censor-in-Chief, Xiao Yu Right Censor-in-Chief, Yang Gongren Minister of Personnel and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Feng Deyi Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚辰，遣岐州刺史柴紹救岷州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengchen the Emperor dispatched Governor Chai Shao of Qizhou to relieve Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengchen the Emperor sent Chai Shao, governor of Qizhou, to relieve Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，吐谷渾及党項寇河州，刺史盧士良擊破之。

translations.literal: On gengyin Tuyuhun together with the Tangut raided Hezhou; Prefect Lu Shiliang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Tuyuhun and the Tangut raided Hezhou. Prefect Lu Shiliang defeated them.

sentences.zh: 丙申，梁師都將辛獠兒引突厥寇林州。

translations.literal: On bingshen Liang Shidu's general Xin Laor led Turks in a raid on Linzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Liang Shidu's general Xin Laor led Turks in a raid on Linzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，苑君彰將高滿政寇代州，驃騎將軍李寶言擊走之。

translations.literal: On wuxu Gao Manzheng, general under Yuan Junzhang, raided Daizhou; General of Agile Cavalry Li Baoyan drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Gao Manzheng, a general under Yuan Junzhang, raided Daizhou. General of Agile Cavalry Li Baoyan drove him off.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，高開道引奚騎寇幽州，長史王詵擊破之。

translations.literal: On guimao, Gao Kaidao led Xi cavalry to raid Youzhou; Chief Administrator Wang Shen defeated and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Gao Kaidao led Xi horsemen against Youzhou; the chief administrator Wang Shen defeated and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥之叛也，突地稽引兵助唐，徙其部落於幽州之昌平城；

translations.literal: When Liu Heita rebelled, Tudu Ji led troops to aid Tang and relocated his tribe to Changping City in Youzhou;
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Heita's rebellion, Tudu Ji had marched to aid the Tang and resettled his people at Changping, near Youzhou;

sentences.zh: 高開道引突厥寇幽州，突地稽將兵邀擊，破之。

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao led the Turks to raid Youzhou; Tudu Ji led troops to intercept and attack, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: when Gao Kaidao led Turks against Youzhou, Tudu Ji intercepted him with his troops and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊午，高滿政以馬邑來降。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuwu, Gao Manzheng surrendered Mayi to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuwu, Gao Manzheng surrendered Mayi to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 先是，前并州總管劉世讓除廣州總管，將之官，上問以備邊之策，世讓對曰：「突厥比數為寇，良以馬邑為之中頓故也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the former Inspector-General of Bingzhou, Liu Shirang, was appointed Inspector-General of Guangzhou and was about to take up his post. The Emperor asked him about strategies for defending the frontier. Shirang replied: "The Turks have repeatedly raided largely because Mayi serves as their middle staging base.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Shirang, the former military governor of Bingzhou, had been appointed governor of Guangzhou and was preparing to take up his post when the Emperor asked him how best to secure the frontier. Shirang answered: "The Turks raid us again and again chiefly because Mayi is their midway supply base.

sentences.zh: 請以勇將戍崞城，多貯金帛，募有降者厚賞之，數出騎兵掠其城下，蹂其禾稼，敗其生業，不出歲餘，彼無所食，必降矣。」

translations.literal: I ask that a brave general be posted to garrison Gao City, store much gold and silk there, offer generous rewards to recruit deserters, and send out cavalry repeatedly to raid beneath their walls, trample their grain crops, and destroy their livelihoods. Within little more than a year they will have nothing to eat and will surely surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Send a bold commander to hold Gao City, stockpile gold and silk, richly reward anyone who defects, and send cavalry out often to harry the countryside below their walls—trampling crops and ruining their livelihood. In little more than a year they will have nothing to eat and must surrender."

sentences.zh: 上然其計，曰：「非公，誰為勇將！」

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his plan and said: "If not you, then who could be the brave general!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the plan and said: "If not you, who else could fill that role!"

sentences.zh: 即命世讓戍崞城，馬邑病之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Shirang to garrison Gao City; Mayi resented this.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered Shirang to garrison Gao City—a move that alarmed Mayi.

sentences.zh: 是時，馬邑人多不願屬突厥，上復遣人招諭苑君璋。

translations.literal: At this time many people in Mayi did not wish to belong to the Turks; the Emperor again sent envoys to win over Yuan Junzhang.
translations.idiomatic: By then many in Mayi no longer wished to remain under Turk rule, and the Emperor again sent envoys to win over Yuan Junzhang.

sentences.zh: 高滿政說君璋盡殺突厥戍兵降唐，君璋不從。

translations.literal: Gao Manzheng urged Junzhang to kill all the Turk garrison troops and surrender to Tang; Junzhang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Manzheng urged Junzhang to slaughter the Turk garrison and surrender to the Tang, but Junzhang refused.

sentences.zh: 滿政因眾心所欲，夜襲君璋，君璋覺之，亡奔突厥，滿政殺君璋之子及突厥戍兵二百人而降。

translations.literal: Manzheng, acting on what the people wanted, attacked Junzhang by night. Junzhang detected it and fled to the Turks. Manzheng killed Junzhang's son and two hundred Turk garrison troops, then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the tide of popular sentiment, Manzheng attacked Junzhang by night. Junzhang discovered the plot and fled to the Turks. Manzheng killed Junzhang's son and two hundred Turk garrison troops, then surrendered to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，梁師都以突厥寇匡州。

translations.literal: On renxu, Liang Shidu led Turks to raid Kuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Liang Shidu led Turk forces against Kuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，苑君璋與突厥吐屯設寇馬邑，高滿政與戰，破之。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Yuan Junzhang together with the Turk Tutun She raided Mayi; Gao Manzheng fought them and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Yuan Junzhang joined the Turk commander Tutun She in an attack on Mayi; Gao Manzheng met them in battle and routed them.

sentences.zh: 以滿政為朔州總管，封榮國公。

translations.literal: Manzheng was appointed Inspector-General of Shuozhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Manzheng was made military governor of Shuozhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.

sentences.zh: 瓜州總管賀若懷廣按部至沙州，值州人張護、李通反，懷廣以數百人保子城；

translations.literal: Inspector-General of Guazhou Heluo Huaiguang was on circuit in Shazhou when the local men Zhang Hu and Li Tong rebelled. Huaiguang defended the inner city with several hundred men;
translations.idiomatic: Heluo Huaiguang, military governor of Guazhou, was on an inspection tour in Shazhou when Zhang Hu and Li Tong of that prefecture rose in revolt. Huaiguang held the inner citadel with a few hundred men;

sentences.zh: 涼州總管楊恭仁遣兵救之，為護等所敗。

translations.literal: Inspector-General of Liangzhou Yang Gongren sent troops to rescue him, but they were defeated by Hu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongren, military governor of Liangzhou, sent a relief force, but Zhang Hu and his followers defeated it.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，柴紹與吐谷渾戰，為其所圍，虜乘高射之，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Chai Shao fought with the Tuyuhun and was surrounded by them. The barbarians shot down from high ground; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Chai Shao clashed with the Tuyuhun and was hemmed in. The enemy, holding the heights, rained arrows down upon him.

sentences.zh: 紹遣人彈胡琵琶，二女子對舞。

translations.literal: Shao had someone play a foreign pipa while two women danced facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Shao ordered a musician to play the pipa while two women danced in paired formation.

sentences.zh: 虜怪之，駐弓矢相與聚觀，紹察其無備，潛遣精騎出虜陳後，擊之，虜眾大潰。

translations.literal: The barbarians found it strange, halted their bowfire, and gathered to watch. Shao saw they were unprepared and secretly sent elite cavalry out behind the enemy lines to strike them; the barbarian host collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun, astonished, lowered their bows and crowded forward to watch. Chai Shao saw his opening and quietly sent picked horsemen around behind the enemy line. When they struck, the Tuyuhun army broke and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙子，苑君璋以突厥寇馬邑，右武候大將軍李高遷及高滿政御之，戰於臘河谷，破之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingzi, Yuan Junzhang led Turks to raid Mayi. Right Wuhou Grand General Li Gaoqian and Gao Manzheng met them, fought at Lagu River, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingzi, Yuan Junzhang led Turks against Mayi. Li Gaoqian, grand general of the Right Wuhou Guard, and Gao Manzheng met them at Lagu River and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 張護、李通殺賀若懷廣，立汝州別駕竇伏明為主，進逼瓜州；

translations.literal: Zhang Hu and Li Tong killed Heluo Huaiguang, installed Dou Fuming, Vice Prefect of Ru Prefecture, as their leader, and advanced to press Guazhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hu and Li Tong killed Heluo Huaiguang, set up Dou Fuming, vice prefect of Ru Prefecture, as their leader, and marched on Guazhou;

sentences.zh: 長史趙孝倫擊卻之。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Zhao Xiaolun attacked and repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Zhao Xiaolun attacked and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 高開道掠赤岸鎮及靈壽、九門、行唐三縣而去。

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao plundered Chi'an Fort and the three counties of Lingshou, Jiumen, and Xingtang, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kaidao raided Chi'an Fort and the counties of Lingshou, Jiumen, and Xingtang, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，崗州刺史馮士翽據新會反，廣州總管劉感討降之，使復其位。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Inspector of Gang Prefecture Feng Shirong seized Xinhui and rebelled. Inspector-General of Guangzhou Liu Gan attacked, accepted his surrender, and restored him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Feng Shirong, prefect of Gangzhou, seized Xinhui and rebelled. Liu Gan, military governor of Guangzhou, suppressed him, accepted his surrender, and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，高開道所部弘陽、統漢二鎮來降。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the two forts of Hongyang and Tonghan under Gao Kaidao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the Hongyang and Tonghan garrisons under Gao Kaidao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 癸未，突厥寇原州；

translations.literal: On guwei, the Turks raided Yuan Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On guwei, the Turks raided Yuan Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，寇朔州。

translations.literal: On yiyou, they raided Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, they raided Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 李高遷為虜所敗，行軍總管尉遲敬德將兵救之。

translations.literal: Li Gaoqian was defeated by the barbarians; Mobile-Campaign General Yuchi Jingde led troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gaoqian was beaten by the enemy; Mobile-Campaign General Yuchi Jingde marched to his relief.

sentences.zh: 巳亥，遣太子將兵屯北邊，秦王世民屯并州，以備突厥。

translations.literal: On sihai, the Crown Prince was sent to lead troops and encamp on the northern frontier; Prince Qin Shimin encamped at Bingzhou to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On sihai, the Crown Prince was ordered north with an army; Prince Qin Li Shimin took up position at Bingzhou to guard against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲辰，突厥寇真州，又寇馬邑。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiachen, the Turks raided Zhen Prefecture and also raided Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiachen, the Turks struck Zhen Prefecture and Mayi.

sentences.zh: 壬子，淮南道行台僕射輔公祏反。

translations.literal: On renzi, Fu Gongshi, Vice Director of the Huainan Circuit Executive Office, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Fu Gongshi, vice director of the Huainan circuit executive office, rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 初，杜伏威與公祏相友善，公祏年長，伏威兄事之，軍中謂之伯父，畏敬與伏威等。

translations.literal: Initially Du Fuwei and Gongshi were close friends. Gongshi was older; Fuwei treated him as an elder brother, and in the army he was called "Uncle," feared and respected equally with Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei and Fu Gongshi had long been close. Gongshi was the elder; Fuwei treated him as an elder brother, and in camp he was called "Uncle," held in the same awe as Fuwei himself.

sentences.zh: 伏威浸忌之，乃署其養子闞稜為左將軍，王雄誕為右將軍，潛奪其兵權。

translations.literal: Fuwei gradually grew wary of him. He appointed his adopted son Kan Ling Left General and Wang Xiongdan Right General, covertly stripping Gongshi of military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei gradually came to distrust him. He appointed his adopted son Kan Ling as left general and Wang Xiongdan as right general, quietly stripping Gongshi of command.

sentences.zh: 公祏知之，怏怏不平，與其故人左遊仙陽為學道辟谷以自晦。

translations.literal: Gongshi knew this and nursed resentful discontent. With his old friend Zuo Youxian he feigned study of the Way and grain abstention to keep a low profile.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi knew it and brooded in sullen resentment. With his old friend Zuo Youxian he pretended to pursue the Way and practice grain abstention, keeping himself out of sight.

sentences.zh: 及伏威入朝，留公祏守丹楊，令雄誕典兵為之副，陰謂雄誕曰：「吾至長安，苟不失職，勿令公祏為變。」

translations.literal: When Fuwei went to court, he left Gongshi to hold Danyang, put Xiongdan in charge of the troops as his deputy, and secretly told Xiongdan: "When I reach Chang'an, if I do not lose my position, do not let Gongshi stir up trouble."
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei went to the capital, he left Gongshi to hold Danyang and put Wang Xiongdan in charge of the army as his deputy, telling him in private: "Once I reach Chang'an, if I keep my post, do not let Gongshi make trouble."

sentences.zh: 伏威既行，左遊仙說公祏謀反；

translations.literal: Once Fuwei had departed, Zuo Youxian urged Gongshi to plot rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: After Fuwei had left, Zuo Youxian urged Gongshi to rebel;

sentences.zh: 而雄誕握兵，公祏不得發。

translations.literal: but Xiongdan held the troops and Gongshi could not act.
translations.idiomatic: but with Xiongdan holding the army, Gongshi could not move.

sentences.zh: 乃詐稱得伏威書，疑雄誕有貳心，雄誕聞之不悅，稱疾不視事；

translations.literal: He then falsely claimed to have received a letter from Fuwei suspecting Xiongdan of disloyalty. Xiongdan, hearing this, was displeased and pleaded illness, refusing to attend to affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi then forged a letter purportedly from Fuwei accusing Xiongdan of disloyalty. Xiongdan, hearing of it, took offense and pleaded illness, refusing to command;

sentences.zh: 公祏因奪其兵，使其黨西門君儀諭以反計。

translations.literal: Gongshi thereupon seized his troops and had his follower Ximen Junyi lay out the rebellion plan to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi seized his troops and sent his follower Ximen Junyi to lay the rebellion plan before him.

sentences.zh: 雄誕始寤而悔之，曰：「今天下方平定，吳王又在京師，大唐兵威，所向無敵，奈何無故自求族滅乎！

translations.literal: Xiongdan finally realized and regretted it, saying: "The realm has just been pacified, the Prince of Wu is in the capital, and Tang arms are invincible wherever they turn—why seek the extermination of your clan for no reason!
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Xiongdan see what was happening, and he repented, saying: "The realm has only just been pacified, the Prince of Wu is in the capital, and Tang arms are irresistible—why court the annihilation of your house for nothing!

sentences.zh: 雄誕有死而已，不敢聞命。

translations.literal: Xiongdan has death alone to offer; I dare not obey such an order.
translations.idiomatic: I, Xiongdan, have only my death to give; I cannot obey you.

sentences.zh: 今從公為逆，不過延百日之命耳，大丈夫安能愛斯須之死，而自陷於不義乎！」

translations.literal: If I follow you in rebellion now, I would gain no more than an extra hundred days of life. How could a true man cling to a moment's breath and plunge himself into disloyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I followed you, I would buy no more than another hundred days. What man worthy of the name would cling to a few breaths of life and throw himself into treason!"

sentences.zh: 公祏知不可屈，縊殺之。

translations.literal: Gongshi knew he could not be swayed and strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not be moved, Gongshi had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 雄誕善撫士卒，得其死力，又約束嚴整，每破城邑，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Xiongdan was skilled at comforting the troops and won their utmost loyalty. His discipline was strict; whenever he took a city or town, he never allowed the slightest harm.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan had a gift for winning soldiers' hearts and commanded their utmost devotion. His discipline was severe; whenever he took a city, not the smallest thing was touched.

sentences.zh: 死之日，江南軍中及民間皆為之流涕。

translations.literal: On the day he died, soldiers throughout Jiangnan and the common people all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, soldiers across Jiangnan and the people alike wept for him.

sentences.zh: 公祏又詐稱伏威不得還江南，貽書令其起兵，大修鎧仗，運糧儲。

translations.literal: Gongshi again falsely claimed that Fuwei could not return to Jiangnan, sent a letter ordering troops raised, and began large-scale repairs of armor and weapons and transport of grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi spread word that Fuwei could not return to Jiangnan, forged a letter calling up the army, and set about repairing armor and stockpiling grain on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 尋稱帝於丹楊，國號宋，修陳故宮室而居之。

translations.literal: Soon he declared himself emperor at Danyang, named his state Song, restored the former palace buildings of Chen, and took up residence there.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he declared himself emperor at Danyang, named his state Song, restored the old Chen palace, and moved in.

sentences.zh: 署置百官，以左遊仙為兵部尚書、東南道大使、越州總管，與張善安連兵，以善安為西南道大行台。

translations.literal: He appointed officials, made Zuo Youxian Minister of War, Grand Envoy of the Southeast Circuit, and Inspector-General of Yue Prefecture, linked forces with Zhang Shan'an, and made Shan'an Grand Executive of the Southwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a full court, made Zuo Youxian minister of war, grand envoy of the southeast circuit, and governor of Yue Prefecture, joined forces with Zhang Shan'an, and appointed Shan'an grand executive of the southwest circuit.

sentences.zh: 己未，突厥寇原州。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the Turks raided Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the Turks raided Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔襄州道行台僕射趙郡王孝恭以舟師趣江州，嶺南道大使李靖以交、廣、泉、桂之眾趣宣州，懷州總管黃君漢出譙、亳，齊州總管李世勣出淮、泗，以討輔公祏。

translations.literal: On yichou, an edict ordered Vice Director of the Xiangzhou Circuit Executive Office Prince Xiaogong of Zhao Commandery to lead the fleet toward Jiang Prefecture; Envoy of the Lingnan Circuit Li Jing to lead the forces of Jiao, Guang, Quan, and Gui toward Xuan Prefecture; Inspector-General of Huaizhou Huang Junhan to advance from Qiao and Bo; and Inspector-General of Qi Prefecture Li Shiji to advance from the Huai and Si Rivers—all to attack Fu Gongshi.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, an edict dispatched Prince Xiaogong of Zhao Commandery, vice director of the Xiangzhou circuit executive office, with a fleet toward Jiang Prefecture; Li Jing, envoy of the Lingnan circuit, with troops from Jiao, Guang, Quan, and Gui toward Xuan Prefecture; Huang Junhan, governor of Huaizhou, from Qiao and Bo; and Li Shiji, governor of Qizhou, from the Huai and Si—all to suppress Fu Gongshi.

sentences.zh: 孝恭將發，與諸將宴集，命取水，忽變為血，在坐皆失色，孝恭舉止自若，曰：「此乃公祏授首之征也！」

translations.literal: As Xiaogong was about to depart, he banqueted with the generals and ordered water fetched; it suddenly turned to blood. Those present all turned pale, but Xiaogong remained composed and said: "This is the omen of Gongshi losing his head!"
translations.idiomatic: As Li Xiaogong was about to set out, he feasted his generals and called for water; it suddenly turned to blood. Every man at the table blanched, but Xiaogong was unperturbed and said: "This is the sign that Gongshi will lose his head!"

sentences.zh: 飲而盡之，眾皆悅服。

translations.literal: He drank it all, and the assembly was heartened and won over.
translations.idiomatic: He drank it down at a gulp, and the company was reassured.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，吐谷渾內附。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Tuyuhun submitted inward to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Tuyuhun submitted to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 辛未，突厥陷原州之善和鎮；

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Turks captured Shanhe Fort in Yuan Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Turks took Shanhe Fort in Yuan Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，又寇渭州。

translations.literal: On guiyou, they again raided Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: on guiyou they raided Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高開道以奚侵幽州，州兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao led the Xi to invade Youzhou; the prefectural troops beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kaidao led Xi forces against Youzhou; the local garrison drove them off.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙子，太子班師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingzi, the Crown Prince withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingzi, the Crown Prince withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 戊子，輔公祏遣其將徐紹宗寇海州，陳政通寇壽陽。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Fu Gongshi sent his generals Xu Shaozong to raid Haizhou and Chen Zhengtong to raid Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Fu Gongshi sent Xu Shaozong against Haizhou and Chen Zhengtong against Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 邛州獠反，遣沛公鄭元□討之。

translations.literal: The Liao of Qiong Prefecture rebelled; the Emperor sent Duke of Pei Zheng Yuan□ to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao of Qiong Prefecture rebelled; the Emperor sent Duke of Pei Zheng Yuan□ to put them down.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，突厥寇幽州。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Turks raided Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the Turks raided Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔以秦王世民為江州道行軍元帥。

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict appointed Prince Qin Shimin Supreme Commander of the Jiangzhou Circuit campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, an edict made Prince Qin Li Shimin supreme commander of the Jiangzhou circuit campaign.

sentences.zh: 乙未，竇伏明以沙州降。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Dou Fuming surrendered Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Dou Fuming surrendered Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 高昌王麴伯雅卒，子文泰立。

translations.literal: King Qu Boya of Gaochang died; his son Wenshu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Boya, king of Gaochang, died; his son Wenshu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 丙申，渝州人張大智反，刺史薛敬仁棄城走。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Zhang Dazhi of Yu Prefecture rebelled; Prefect Xue Jingren abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zhang Dazhi of Yu Prefecture rebelled; Prefect Xue Jingren abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，高開道引突厥二萬騎寇幽州。

translations.literal: On renyin, Gao Kaidao led twenty thousand Turk cavalry to raid Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Gao Kaidao led twenty thousand Turk horsemen against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥惡弘農公劉世讓為己患，遣其臣曹般阤來，言世讓與可汗通謀，欲為亂，上信之。

translations.literal: The Turks regarded Duke of Hongnong Liu Shirang as a menace and sent their minister Cao Banduo to say that Shirang was in secret league with the qaghan plotting rebellion. The Emperor believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks hated Liu Shirang, Duke of Hongnong, as a threat and sent their minister Cao Banduo to claim that Shirang was conspiring with the qaghan to rebel. The Emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午，殺世讓，籍其家。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingwu, Shirang was executed and his household properties confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingwu, Liu Shirang was executed and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民猶在并州，己未，詔世民引軍還。

translations.literal: Prince Qin Shimin was still at Bingzhou. On jiwei, an edict ordered Shimin to lead his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qin Li Shimin was still at Bingzhou when, on jiwei, an edict ordered him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 上幸華陰。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor traveled to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 張大智侵涪州，刺史田世康等討之，大智以眾降。

translations.literal: Zhang Dazhi invaded Fu Prefecture; Prefect Tian Shikang and others attacked him, and Dazhi surrendered with his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dazhi raided Fu Prefecture; Prefect Tian Shikang and others attacked him, and Dazhi surrendered with his force.

sentences.zh: 初，上遣右武候大將軍李高遷助朔州總管高滿政守馬邑，苑君璋引突厥萬餘騎至城下，滿政擊破之。

translations.literal: Initially the Emperor sent Right Wuhou Grand General Li Gaoqian to assist Inspector-General of Shuozhou Gao Manzheng in defending Mayi. Yuan Junzhang led more than ten thousand Turk cavalry to the foot of the walls; Manzheng defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had sent Li Gaoqian, grand general of the Right Wuhou Guard, to help Gao Manzheng, governor of Shuozhou, hold Mayi. Yuan Junzhang brought more than ten thousand Turk horsemen to the walls; Manzheng beat them off.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗怒，大發兵攻馬邑。

translations.literal: Qaghan Jieli flew into a rage and mobilized a large force to attack Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Jieli was furious and raised a great army to besiege Mayi.

sentences.zh: 高遷懼，帥所部二千人斬關宵遁，虜邀之，失亡者半。

translations.literal: Gaoqian, in fear, led his two thousand men to cut through the gate and flee by night. The barbarians intercepted them; half were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Gaoqian broke out at night with his two thousand men. The Turks cut off their retreat; half his force was lost.

sentences.zh: 頡利自帥眾攻城，滿政出兵御之，或一日戰十餘合。

translations.literal: Jieli personally led the host in besieging the city. Manzheng sent troops out to meet them; sometimes they fought more than ten engagements in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli himself led the siege. Manzheng sallied forth to meet him; some days they fought more than ten times.

sentences.zh: 上命行軍總管劉世讓救之，至松子嶺，不敢進，還保崞城。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Mobile-Campaign General Liu Shirang to rescue the city. When he reached Songzi Ridge he dared not advance and withdrew to hold Gao City.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Liu Shirang, mobile-campaign general, to relieve the city. At Songzi Ridge he halted and would not go forward, falling back to hold Gao City.

sentences.zh: 會頡利遣使求婚，上曰：「釋馬邑之圍，乃可議婚。」

translations.literal: Just then Jieli sent envoys to request a marriage alliance. The Emperor said: "Lift the siege of Mayi, and only then may we discuss marriage."
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Jieli sent envoys to propose a marriage alliance. The Emperor replied: "Raise the siege of Mayi, and then we may speak of marriage."

sentences.zh: 頡利慾解兵，義成公主固請攻之。

translations.literal: Jieli wished to withdraw his troops, but Princess Yicheng strongly urged him to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli was inclined to withdraw, but Princess Yicheng pressed him hard to continue the assault.

sentences.zh: 頡利以高開道善為攻具，召開道，與之攻馬邑甚急。

translations.literal: Jieli, because Gao Kaidao was skilled at siege engines, summoned Kaidao and with him pressed the attack on Mayi very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Gao Kaidao's skill with siege engines, Jieli summoned him and together they pressed the attack on Mayi with terrible force.

sentences.zh: 頡利誘滿政使降，滿政罵之。

translations.literal: Jieli tried to induce Manzheng to surrender; Manzheng reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli tried to win Manzheng over; Manzheng cursed him.

sentences.zh: 糧且盡，救兵未至，滿政欲潰圍走朔州，右虞候杜士遠以虜兵盛，恐不免，壬戌，殺滿政降於突厥，苑君璋復殺城中豪傑與滿政同謀者三十餘人。

translations.literal: Provisions were nearly exhausted and relief had not come. Manzheng wished to break out and flee to Shuozhou. Right Yuhou Du Shiyuan, fearing that with the barbarian forces so strong they could not escape, on renxu killed Manzheng and surrendered to the Turks. Yuan Junzhang also killed more than thirty notables in the city who had plotted with Manzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grain was running out and no relief came. Manzheng planned to break out toward Shuozhou. Du Shiyuan, right yuhou, fearing that with the enemy so strong escape was impossible, on renxu killed Manzheng and surrendered to the Turks. Yuan Junzhang then executed more than thirty leading men in the city who had plotted with him.

sentences.zh: 上以滿政子玄積為上柱國，襲爵。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Manzheng's son Xuanji a Supreme Pillar of State, inheriting the title.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Manzheng's son Xuanji a supreme pillar of state, allowing him to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，突厥復請和親，以馬邑歸唐；

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Turks again requested a marriage alliance and returned Mayi to Tang;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the Turks again sought peace by marriage and restored Mayi to the Tang;

sentences.zh: 上以將軍秦武通為朔州總管。

translations.literal: the Emperor appointed General Qin Wutong Inspector-General of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor appointed General Qin Wutong military governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥數為邊患，并州大總管府長史竇靜表請於太原置屯田，以省饋運；

translations.literal: The Turks repeatedly troubled the border. Chief Secretary of the Bingzhou Grand Inspectorate Dou Jing memorialized requesting that military colonies be established at Taiyuan to reduce transport of supplies;
translations.idiomatic: With the Turks raiding the frontier again and again, Dou Jing, chief secretary of the Bingzhou grand inspectorate, memorialized to establish military colonies at Taiyuan and cut supply transport;

sentences.zh: 議者以為煩擾，不許。

translations.literal: discussants thought it would be burdensome and it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: critics called the plan too disruptive, and it was rejected.

sentences.zh: 靜切論不已，敕征靜入朝，使與裴寂、蕭瑀、封德彝相論難於上前，寂等不能屈，乃從靜議，歲收數千斛，上善之，命檢校并州大總管。

translations.literal: Jing argued forcefully without cease. An edict summoned Jing to court and had him debate before the Emperor with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Deyi. Ji and the others could not refute him, and the Emperor adopted Jing's proposal. Each year several thousand hu were harvested. The Emperor approved and appointed him Acting Grand Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jing pressed his case relentlessly. The Emperor summoned him to court and had him debate Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Deyi before the throne. None could overcome his arguments, and the plan was adopted; each year several thousand hu of grain were harvested. The Emperor was pleased and made him acting grand inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 靜，抗之子也。

translations.literal: Jing was the son of Dou Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jing was the son of Dou Kang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛巳，秦王世民復請增置屯田於并州之境，從之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinsi, Prince Qin Shimin again requested adding military colonies within Bingzhou territory; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinsi, Prince Qin Li Shimin again asked to expand military colonies in Bingzhou; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 黃州總管周法明將兵擊輔公祏，張善安據夏口，拒之。

translations.literal: Inspector-General of Huang Prefecture Zhou Faming led troops against Fu Gongshi. Zhang Shan'an held Xiakou and blocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Faming, military governor of Huang Prefecture, marched against Fu Gongshi. Zhang Shan'an held Xiakou and barred his way.

sentences.zh: 法明屯荊口鎮，壬午，法明登戰艦飲酒，善安遣刺客數人詐乘魚鰈而至，見者不以為虞，遂殺法明而去。

translations.literal: Faming encamped at Jingkou Fort. On renwu, Faming went aboard a warship to drink wine. Shan'an sent several assassins who pretended to arrive in fishing boats; onlookers suspected nothing, and they killed Faming and left.
translations.idiomatic: Faming encamped at Jingkou Fort. On renwu he went aboard a warship to drink. Shan'an sent several assassins disguised in boats laden with salted fish; no one thought anything of it, and they killed Faming and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 甲申，舒州總管張鎮周等擊輔公祏將陳當世於猷州之黃沙，大破之。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Inspector-General of Shu Prefecture Zhang Zhenzhou and others struck Fu Gongshi's general Chen Dangshi at Huangsha in You Prefecture and routed them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Zhang Zhenzhou, military governor of Shu Prefecture, and others defeated Fu Gongshi's general Chen Dangshi at Huangsha in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上校獵於華陰。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Emperor conducted a hunting review at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Emperor held a hunting review at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 己丑，迎勞秦王世民於忠武頓。

translations.literal: On jichou, he went to Zhongwu Post to welcome and honor Prince Qin Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, he went to Zhongwu Post to welcome Prince Qin Li Shimin.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸卯，安撫使李大亮誘張善安，執之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on guimao, Pacification Commissioner Li Daliang enticed Zhang Shannan and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guimao, pacification commissioner Li Daliang lured Zhang Shannan into his hands and arrested him.

sentences.zh: 大亮擊善安於洪州，與善安隔水而陳，遙相與語。

translations.literal: Daliang attacked Shannan at Hongzhou; he and Shannan drew up on opposite banks of the water and spoke to each other from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang pressed Shannan at Hongzhou. They encamped on opposite banks and called back and forth across the river.

sentences.zh: 大亮諭以禍福，善安曰：「善安初無反心，正為將士所誤；

translations.literal: Daliang explained fortune and calamity to him. Shannan said, "I never had a rebellious heart to begin with—I was misled by my officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Daliang laid out the stakes. Shannan replied, "I never meant to rebel in the first place—my officers and men led me astray;

sentences.zh: 欲降又恐不免。」

translations.literal: I wish to surrender but fear I will not be spared."
translations.idiomatic: I want to submit, but I am afraid I will not escape punishment."

sentences.zh: 大亮曰：「張總管有降心，則與我一家耳。」

translations.literal: Daliang said, "If Commandant Zhang has a mind to surrender, then he and I are one family."
translations.idiomatic: Daliang said, "If Commandant Zhang is ready to surrender, then he and I are on the same side."

sentences.zh: 因單騎渡水入其陳，與善安執手共語，示無猜間。

translations.literal: Thereupon alone on horseback he crossed the water into their formation, clasped Shannan's hand, and spoke with him, showing he harbored no suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode across the river alone into the enemy camp, took Shannan's hand, and spoke with him openly to show he had no mistrust.

sentences.zh: 善安大悅，遂許之降。

translations.literal: Shannan was greatly pleased and thereupon agreed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan was delighted and agreed to submit.

sentences.zh: 既而善安將數十騎詣大亮營，大亮止其騎於門外，引善安入，與語，久之，善安辭去，大亮命武士執之，從騎皆走。

translations.literal: Before long Shannan came to Daliang's camp with several dozen horsemen. Daliang kept the horsemen outside the gate and led Shannan inside to converse. After a long while Shannan took his leave; Daliang ordered warriors to seize him, and the escorting horsemen all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shannan rode to Daliang's camp with several dozen men. Daliang kept the escort outside the gate and led Shannan in to talk. After a long conversation Shannan rose to leave—but Daliang ordered his guards to seize him, and the horsemen fled.

sentences.zh: 善安營中聞之，大怒，悉眾而來，將攻大亮。

translations.literal: When Shannan's camp heard of this, they were greatly angry, mustered all their forces, and were about to attack Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shannan's troops learned what had happened, they flew into a rage, mustered their full strength, and marched to attack Daliang.

sentences.zh: 大亮使人諭之曰：「吾不留總管。

translations.literal: Daliang sent someone to instruct them, saying, "I am not detaining the Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang sent a messenger to explain: "I am not holding the Commandant against his will.

sentences.zh: 總管赤心歸國，謂我曰：『若還營，恐將士或有異同，為其所制。』

translations.literal: The Commandant is sincerely returning to the state and told me: 'If I return to camp, I fear the officers and soldiers may disagree and I will be controlled by them.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant is returning to the Tang in good faith and told me, 'If I go back to camp, my men may not all agree, and I will be at their mercy.'

sentences.zh: 故自留不去耳，卿輩何怒於我！」

translations.literal: That is why he chose to stay of his own accord and not leave—why are you angry with me!"
translations.idiomatic: That is why he chose to stay here himself—why are you furious with me!"

sentences.zh: 其黨復大罵曰：「張總管賣我以自媚於人。」

translations.literal: His followers again cursed loudly: "Commandant Zhang has sold us out to curry favor with others."
translations.idiomatic: His men cried out in outrage: "Commandant Zhang has sold us out to win favor with the Tang!"

sentences.zh: 遂皆潰去。

translations.literal: Thereupon they all dispersed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: With that they all broke up and scattered.

sentences.zh: 大亮追擊，多所虜獲。

translations.literal: Daliang pursued and struck; he captured many prisoners and booty.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang gave chase and took many prisoners and spoils.

sentences.zh: 送善安於長安，善安自稱不與輔公祏交通，上赦其罪，善遇之；

translations.literal: He sent Shannan to Chang'an. Shannan declared he had had no dealings with Fu Gongshi; the Emperor pardoned his crime and treated him well;
translations.idiomatic: Daliang sent Shannan to Chang'an. Shannan insisted he had never colluded with Fu Gongshi, and the emperor pardoned him and treated him kindly;

sentences.zh: 及公祏敗，得所與往還書，乃殺之。

translations.literal: when Gongshi was defeated, correspondence between them was recovered, and Shannan was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: but when Gongshi fell, letters exchanged between them came to light, and the emperor had him executed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，車駕至長安。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the imperial carriage arrived at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the Emperor entered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 己巳，突厥寇定州，州兵擊走之。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Turks raided Dingzhou; the prefecture's troops struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Turks raided Dingzhou; local forces beat them back.

sentences.zh: 庚申，白簡、白狗羌並遣使入貢。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Baijian and Baigou Qiang both dispatched envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the Baijian and Baigou Qiang sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，依周、齊舊制，每州置大中正一人，掌知州內人物，品量望第，以本州門望高者領之，無品秩。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, following the old systems of Zhou and Qi, one Chief Rectifier was established in each prefecture to oversee the persons within the prefecture, assess their standing and rank, with the assignment held by those of the highest family prestige in the prefecture, without official rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, following the old Zhou and Qi practice, the court appointed one Chief Rectifier in each prefecture to assess the standing and pedigree of local families. The post went to men of the highest local prestige and carried no official rank.

sentences.zh: 壬午，趙郡王孝恭擊輔公祏別將於樅陽，破之。

translations.literal: On renwu, Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong struck Fu Gongshi's lieutenant general at Zongyang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong defeated a lieutenant of Fu Gongshi at Zongyang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，鄒州人鄧同穎殺刺史李士衡反。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Deng Tongying of Zouzhou killed Prefect Li Shiheng and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Deng Tongying of Zouzhou killed Prefect Li Shiheng and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以白狗等羌地置維、恭二州。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the territory of the Baigou and other Qiang was made into the two prefectures of Wei and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the court created the prefectures of Wei and Gong from Baigou Qiang territory.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛丑，輔公祏遣兵圍猷州，刺史左難當嬰城自守。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinchou, Fu Gongshi dispatched troops to besiege Youzhou; Prefect Zuo Nandang held the city and defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinchou, Fu Gongshi sent troops to besiege Youzhou; Prefect Zuo Nandang locked the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 安撫使李大亮引兵擊公祏，破之。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Li Daliang led troops to strike Gongshi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Li Daliang marched against Gongshi and routed him.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭攻公祏鵲頭鎮，拔之。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong attacked Gongshi's Queshi garrison and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong captured Gongshi's Queshi garrison.

sentences.zh: 丁未，高麗王建武遣使來請班歷。

translations.literal: On dingwei, King Jianwu of Goryeo dispatched envoys to request the imperial calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei King Jianwu of Goryeo sent envoys asking to receive the Tang calendar.

sentences.zh: 遣使冊建武為遼東郡王、高麗王；

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to invest Jianwu as Prince of Liaodong Commandery and King of Goryeo;
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to invest Jianwu as Prince of Liaodong Commandery and King of Goryeo;

sentences.zh: 以百濟王夫餘璋為帶方郡王，新羅王金真平為樂浪郡王。

translations.literal: King Buyeo Jang of Baekje was made Prince of Daifang Commandery, and King Kim Jeongpyeong of Silla was made Prince of Lelang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo Jang of Baekje was named Prince of Daifang Commandery, and Kim Jeongpyeong of Silla was named Prince of Lelang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 始州獠反，遣行台僕射竇軌討之。

translations.literal: The Liao of Shizhou rebelled; Regional Secretariat Vice Director Dou Gui was dispatched to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao of Shizhou rose in revolt, and the court sent Regional Secretariat Vice Director Dou Gui to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 己酉，詔：「諸州有明一經以上未仕者，鹹以名聞；

translations.literal: On jiyou, an edict declared: "In all prefectures, those who have mastered one Classic or more but have not yet held office—all are to be reported by name;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou an edict declared: "In every prefecture, report the names of all men who have mastered at least one Classic but have not yet entered office;

sentences.zh: 州縣及鄉皆置學。」

translations.literal: in prefectures, counties, and townships schools are all to be established."
translations.idiomatic: and establish schools in every prefecture, county, and township."

sentences.zh: 壬子，行軍副總管權文誕破輔公祏之黨於猷州，拔其枚洄等四鎮。

translations.literal: On renzi, Deputy Campaign Commander Quan Wengan defeated Fu Gongshi's faction at Youzhou and captured four garrisons including Meihui.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Deputy Campaign Commander Quan Wengan defeated Fu Gongshi's forces at Youzhou and captured four garrisons, including Meihui.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上幸國子學，釋奠；

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and performed the libation rite;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and offered libations to Confucius;

sentences.zh: 詔諸王公子弟各就學。

translations.literal: an edict ordered all princes' sons and younger brothers to enroll in study.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered all princes' sons and younger brothers to enroll in school.

sentences.zh: 戊午，改大總管為大都督府。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Great Regional Commanders were renamed Grand Area Commander Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the court renamed Great Regional Commanders as Grand Area Commander Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 己未，高開道將張金樹殺開道來降。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Gao Kaidao's general Zhang Jinshu killed Kaidao and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Gao Kaidao's general Zhang Jinshu killed Kaidao and submitted to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 開道見天下皆定，欲降，自以數反覆，不敢；

translations.literal: Kaidao saw that all under heaven was settled and wished to surrender, but because he had repeatedly changed sides, he did not dare;
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao saw the realm at peace and wanted to surrender, but having switched allegiance so many times, he did not dare;

sentences.zh: 且恃突厥之眾，遂無降意。

translations.literal: moreover he relied on the numbers of the Turks, and so had no mind to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: moreover he counted on Turkic support, and so put surrender out of his mind.

sentences.zh: 其將卒皆山東人，思鄉里，咸有離心。

translations.literal: His officers and soldiers were all men from Shandong, homesick for their native places, and all nursed thoughts of departure.
translations.idiomatic: His officers and soldiers were all men from Shandong, homesick and restless, and all nursed thoughts of leaving.

sentences.zh: 開道選勇敢士數百，謂之假子，常直閣內，使金樹領之。

translations.literal: Kaidao selected several hundred brave warriors, calling them his foster sons, who were always on duty inside the pavilion; he had Jinshu command them.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao picked several hundred brave warriors, called them his foster sons, and kept them on constant guard inside his pavilion under Jinshu's command.

sentences.zh: 故劉黑闥將張君立亡在開道所，與金樹密謀取開道。

translations.literal: Former Liu Heita general Zhang Junli, who had fled and was staying with Kaidao, secretly plotted with Jinshu to seize Kaidao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Junli, a former general of Liu Heita who had taken refuge with Kaidao, secretly plotted with Jinshu to kill him.

sentences.zh: 金樹遣其黨數人入閣內，與假子遊戲，向夕，潛斷其弓弦，藏刀槊於床下，合暝，抱之趨出，金樹帥其黨大噪，攻開道閣，假子將御之，而弓弦皆絕，刀槊已失，爭出降；

translations.literal: Jinshu sent several of his followers into the pavilion to play with the foster sons. Toward evening they secretly cut the bowstrings, hid blades and spears beneath the beds, and at dusk seized the foster sons and rushed out. Jinshu led his followers in a great uproar and assaulted Kaidao's pavilion. The foster sons tried to defend themselves, but all their bowstrings were broken and their blades and spears were gone; they scrambled out to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu sent several of his men into the pavilion to play with the foster sons. Toward evening they secretly cut the bowstrings and hid blades and spears under the beds. At dusk they seized the foster sons and rushed out. Jinshu led his followers in a great clamor and stormed Kaidao's pavilion. The foster sons tried to fight back, but their bowstrings were all cut and their weapons gone; they scrambled out to surrender;

sentences.zh: 君立亦舉火於外與相應，內外惶擾。

translations.literal: Junli also raised fires outside in concert, and within and without there was panic and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Junli also lit fires outside in concert, and panic spread within and without.

sentences.zh: 開道知不免，乃擐甲持兵坐堂上，與妻妾奏樂酣飲，眾憚其勇，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Kaidao knew he could not escape; he donned armor, took up arms, and sat in the hall, drinking heavily while his wives and concubines played music. The men feared his courage and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Kaidao donned armor, took up his weapons, and sat in the hall drinking heavily while his wives and concubines played music. The men feared his ferocity and did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 天且明，開道縊妻妾及諸子，乃自殺。

translations.literal: As dawn approached, Kaidao strangled his wives, concubines, and sons, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: As dawn neared, Kaidao strangled his wives, concubines, and sons, then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 金樹陳兵，悉收假子斬之，並殺君立，死者五百餘人。

translations.literal: Jinshu deployed his troops, rounded up all the foster sons and beheaded them, and also killed Junli; more than five hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu deployed his troops, rounded up all the foster sons and beheaded them, and killed Junli as well; more than five hundred died.

sentences.zh: 遣使來降，詔以其地置媯州。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to surrender; an edict established the territory as Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to surrender, and an edict established his territory as Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以金樹為北燕州都督。

translations.literal: On renxu, Jinshu was appointed Area Commander of Beiyan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Jinshu was appointed Area Commander of Beiyan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，洋、集二州獠反，陷隆州晉城。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Liao of Yang and Ji prefectures rebelled and captured Jincheng in Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the Liao of Yang and Ji prefectures rebelled and captured Jincheng in Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 是月，太保吳王杜伏威薨。

translations.literal: That month, Grand Preceptor Prince Wu Du Fuwei died.
translations.idiomatic: That month Grand Preceptor Prince Wu Du Fuwei died.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏之反也，詐稱伏威之命以紿其眾。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, he falsely claimed to be acting on Fuwei's orders to deceive his followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, he falsely claimed to be acting on Fuwei's orders to deceive his followers.

sentences.zh: 及公祏平，趙郡王孝恭不知其詐，以狀聞；

translations.literal: When Gongshi was pacified, Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong, not knowing it was a fraud, reported the matter;
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi was defeated, Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong, not knowing it was a fraud, reported the matter;

sentences.zh: 詔追除伏威名，籍沒其妻子。

translations.literal: an edict stripped Fuwei posthumously of his rank and confiscated his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict posthumously stripped Fuwei of his rank and confiscated his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，知其冤，赦之，復其官爵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, knowing he had been wronged, he pardoned him and restored his rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he recognized the injustice, pardoned Fuwei, and restored his rank and titles.

sentences.zh: 三月，初定令，以太尉、司徒、司空為三公，次尚書、門下、中書、秘書、殿中、內侍為六省，次御史台，次太常至太府為九寺，次將作監，次國子學，次天策上將府，次左、右衛至左、右領衛為十四衛；

translations.literal: In the third month, the statutes were first established. The Grand Minister, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works were made the Three Excellencies. Next came the six departments: Secretariat, Chancellery, Palace Secretariat, Imperial Library, Palace Administration, and Inner Attendants. Next the Censorate. Next the nine directorates from Grand Ritual Master to Grand Treasury. Next the Directorate of Imperial Works. Next the Imperial Academy. Next the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Headquarters. Next the fourteen guards from Left and Right Guard to Left and Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court first established the new statutes. The Grand Minister, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works became the Three Excellencies. Next came the six departments—the Secretariat, Chancellery, Palace Secretariat, Imperial Library, Palace Administration, and Inner Attendants—followed by the Censorate, the nine directorates from Grand Ritual Master to Grand Treasury, the Directorate of Imperial Works, the Imperial Academy, the Heavenly Stratagem General-in-Chief Headquarters, and the fourteen guards from Left and Right Guard to Left and Right Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 東宮置三師、三少、詹事及兩坊、三寺、十率府；

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace was given Three Preceptors, Three Junior Preceptors, the Grand Mentor, two workshops, three offices, and ten command offices;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was given Three Preceptors, Three Junior Preceptors, a Grand Mentor, two workshops, three offices, and ten command offices;

sentences.zh: 王、公置府佐、國官，公主置邑司，並為京職事官。

translations.literal: princes and dukes were given household aides and state officials, princesses were given fief administrators—all as capital duty officials.
translations.idiomatic: princes and dukes were given household aides and state officials, and princesses were given fief administrators—all counted as capital duty officials.

sentences.zh: 州、縣、鎮、戌為外職事官。

translations.literal: Prefectures, counties, garrison towns, and frontier posts were external duty officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, counties, garrison towns, and frontier posts were external duty officials.

sentences.zh: 自開府議同三司至將仕郎二十八隊，為文散官；

translations.literal: From Opener of the Government with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies through Expectant Gentleman, twenty-eight ranks were civil honorary offices;
translations.idiomatic: From Opener of the Government with Equal Privilege to the Three Excellencies through Expectant Gentleman, twenty-eight ranks were civil honorary offices;

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍至陪戎副尉三十一階，為武散官；

translations.literal: from General of Fast Cavalry through Assistant Frontier Guard, thirty-one grades were military honorary offices;
translations.idiomatic: from General of Fast Cavalry through Assistant Frontier Guard, thirty-one grades were military honorary offices;

sentences.zh: 上柱國至武騎尉十二等，為勳官。

translations.literal: from Supreme Pillar of State to Martial Cavalry Officer, twelve grades were merit offices.
translations.idiomatic: from Supreme Pillar of State to Martial Cavalry Officer, twelve grades were merit offices.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，趙郡王孝恭破輔公祏於蕪湖，拔梁山等三鎮。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong defeated Fu Gongshi at Wuhu and captured three garrisons including Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong defeated Fu Gongshi at Wuhu and captured three garrisons, including Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，安撫使任瑰拔揚子城，廣陵城主龍龕降。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Pacification Commissioner Ren Gui captured Yangzi City, and Long Kan, lord of Guangling City, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Pacification Commissioner Ren Gui captured Yangzi City, and Long Kan, lord of Guangling, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，突厥寇原州。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Turks raided Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the Turks raided Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，趙郡王孝恭克丹楊。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong captured Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong captured Danyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，輔公祏遣其將馮慧亮、陳當世將舟師三萬屯博望山，陳正通、徐紹宗將步騎二萬屯青林山，仍於梁山連鐵鎖以斷江路，築卻月城，延袤十餘里，又結壘江西以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Previously, Fu Gongshi had sent his generals Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi to lead thirty thousand naval troops to encamp at Bowang Mountain, and Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Qinglin Mountain. They further linked iron chains across the Yangtze at Liangshan to block the water route, built a crescent-shaped fort stretching more than ten li, and also established fortifications west of the river to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fu Gongshi had posted Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi with thirty thousand naval troops at Bowang Mountain, and Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry at Qinglin Mountain. They further stretched iron chains across the Yangtze at Liangshan to block the river, built a crescent-shaped fort more than ten li long, and raised fortifications west of the river to hold off the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 孝恭與李靖帥舟師次舒州，李世勣帥步卒一萬渡淮，拔壽陽，次硤石。

translations.literal: Xiaogong and Li Jing led the fleet to camp at Shuzhou. Li Shiji led ten thousand foot soldiers across the Huai, captured Shouyang, and encamped at Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong and Li Jing led the fleet to Shuzhou. Li Shiji crossed the Huai with ten thousand foot soldiers, captured Shouyang, and encamped at Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 慧亮等堅壁不戰，孝恭遣奇兵絕其糧道，慧亮等軍乏食，夜，遣兵薄孝恭營，孝恭安臥不動。

translations.literal: Huiliang and the others held their walls and would not fight. Xiaogong sent picked troops to cut off their supply lines. When Huiliang's army ran short of food, at night they sent troops to press close to Xiaogong's camp; Xiaogong lay at ease and did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Huiliang and the others held their fortifications and refused battle. Xiaogong sent picked troops to cut their supply lines. When their army ran short of food, they sent troops by night to probe Xiaogong's camp; Xiaogong lay still and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 孝恭集諸將議軍事，皆曰：「慧亮等擁強兵，據水陸之險，攻之不可猝拔，不如直指丹楊，掩其巢穴。

translations.literal: Xiaogong gathered the generals to discuss the campaign. All said: "Huiliang and the others command strong forces and hold the advantages of water and land. An assault cannot quickly succeed. Better to march straight on Danyang and strike at their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong gathered his generals to discuss strategy. All said, "Huiliang and the others hold strong forces and the advantages of land and water. We cannot take them quickly. Better to march straight on Danyang and strike at their nest.

sentences.zh: 丹楊既潰，慧亮等自降矣！」

translations.literal: If Danyang falls, Huiliang and the others will surrender of themselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Once Danyang falls, Huiliang and the others will surrender of their own accord!"

sentences.zh: 孝恭將從其議，李靖曰：「公祏精兵雖在此水陸二軍，然後自將亦為不少，今博望諸柵尚不能拔，公祏保據石頭，豈易取哉！

translations.literal: Xiaogong was about to follow this advice when Li Jing said: "Although Gongshi's elite troops are in these two land and water armies, the troops he leads in person are also considerable. If we cannot even capture the fortifications at Bowang, can we easily take Gongshi entrenched at Shitou?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong was about to follow this plan when Li Jing said, "Although Gongshi's best troops are in these two armies, the force he leads in person is also considerable. If we cannot even take the fortifications at Bowang, how easily can we seize Gongshi entrenched at Shitou?

sentences.zh: 進攻丹楊，旬月不下，慧亮等躡吾後，腹背受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: Striking at Danyang, if we do not take it in a month, Huiliang and the others will follow at our rear—we will be attacked front and back. That is the path to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: If we march on Danyang and fail to take it within a month, Huiliang and the others will follow at our rear and we will be caught between two enemies. That is the road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 慧亮、正通皆百戰餘賊，其心非不欲戰，正以公祏立計使之持重，欲以老我師耳。

translations.literal: Huiliang and Zhengtong are both battle-hardened rebels. It is not that they do not wish to fight; Gongshi's plan deliberately keeps them steady so they can wear our army down.
translations.idiomatic: Huiliang and Zhengtong are both battle-hardened rebels. It is not that they do not want to fight; Gongshi's plan deliberately keeps them steady so they can wear our army down.

sentences.zh: 我今攻其城以挑之，一舉可破也！」

translations.literal: If we now assault their fort to provoke them, we can break them in one stroke!"
translations.idiomatic: If we assault their fort now and provoke them into battle, we can break them in one stroke!"

sentences.zh: 孝恭然之，使羸兵先攻賊壘而勒精兵結陳以待之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong agreed. He had weak troops attack the rebel fort first while keeping his elite forces in battle array to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong agreed. He sent weak troops to attack the rebel fort first while keeping his elite forces in battle formation to await them.

sentences.zh: 攻壘者不勝而走，賊出兵追之，行數里，遇大軍，與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: The attackers did not prevail and fled. The rebels sallied out in pursuit; after several li they met the main army, fought, and were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The attackers failed and fled. The rebels sallied out in pursuit; after several li they ran into the main army, fought, and were utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 闞稜免冑謂賊眾曰：「汝曹不識我邪？

translations.literal: Kan Ling removed his helmet and called to the rebel ranks: "Do you not know me?
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ling removed his helmet and shouted to the rebel ranks, "Don't you know who I am?

sentences.zh: 何敢來與我戰！」

translations.literal: How dare you come fight me!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you come fight me!"

sentences.zh: 賊眾多稜故部曲，皆無鬥志，或有拜者，由是遂敗。

translations.literal: Many in the rebel ranks had been Kan's former subordinates; they all lacked fighting spirit, and some even bowed to him—thus they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the rebel ranks had once served under Kan; they lost all will to fight, and some even bowed to him—thus the rebels were defeated.

sentences.zh: 孝恭、靖乘勝逐北，轉戰百餘里，博山、青林兩戍皆潰，慧亮、正通等遁歸，殺傷及溺死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Xiaogong and Jing pressed the victory in pursuit, fighting over a hundred li. The garrisons at Boshan and Qinglin both collapsed. Huiliang, Zhengtong, and the others fled back. Killed, wounded, and drowned numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong and Jing pressed the victory in pursuit, fighting for more than a hundred li. The garrisons at Boshan and Qinglin both collapsed. Huiliang, Zhengtong, and the others fled back. Killed, wounded, and drowned numbered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 李靖兵先至丹楊，公祏大懼，擁兵數萬，棄城東走，欲就左遊仙於會稽，李世勣追之。

translations.literal: Li Jing's troops reached Danyang first. Gongshi was greatly afraid. Leading tens of thousands of troops, he abandoned the city and fled east, intending to join Zuo Youxian at Kuaiji; Li Shiji pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's troops reached Danyang first. Gongshi was terrified. Leading tens of thousands of men, he abandoned the city and fled east toward Zuo Youxian at Kuaiji; Li Shiji pursued him.

sentences.zh: 公祏至句容，從兵能屬者才五百人，夜，宿常州，其將吳騷等謀執之。

translations.literal: When Gongshi reached Jurong, only about five hundred followers could keep up. At night he lodged at Changzhou; his generals Wu Sao and others plotted to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Gongshi reached Jurong, only about five hundred followers could keep up. That night he lodged at Changzhou, where his generals Wu Sao and others plotted to seize him.

sentences.zh: 公祏覺之，棄妻子，獨將腹心數十人，斬關走。

translations.literal: Gongshi detected it, abandoned his wife and children, and with only several dozen trusted men broke through the gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi detected the plot, abandoned his wife and children, and with only several dozen trusted men broke through the gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 至武康，為野人所攻，西門君儀戰死。

translations.literal: When he reached Wukang, he was attacked by locals; Ximen Junyi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Wukang he was attacked by locals; Ximen Junyi died fighting.

sentences.zh: 執公祏，送丹楊梟首，分捕餘黨，悉誅之，江南皆平。
